conclusion: The Clear Human Web offers a cryptographic access-control and privacy framework for proving personhood online, but it is classical security/privacy engineering rather than quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Cross-Modal Semantic Successive Refinement For Generative Image Communication Over Underwater Acoustic Channels
authors: Xu Pei, Bin Wang, Guangxu Zhu, Yi Zhang, Haiyan Fan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Underwater acoustic communication faces challenges such as limited available bandwidth and complex channel environments, which impose demanding requirements on efficient image transmission and reliable reconstruction. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a generative image communication framework based on cross-modal semantic successive refinement. At the transmitter, text descriptions, compact bottleneck features, and visual side information compressed by residual vector quantization are transmitted. At the receiver, text and bottleneck features are first fused to predict a base estimate of the intermediate visual representation. The received RVQ indices are then used to recover supplementary visual information and perform residual correction, followed by image reconstruction using a one-step Pixel Mean Flow model. During training, a CLIP-based text-image semantic consistency constraint is introduced to preserve the semantic correspondence between generated results and the original text descriptions. During transmission, protection resources are allocated according to the importance of different information branches and RVQ quantization stages. Simulations using COCO 2017 images and measured underwater acoustic channel records from Watermark show that text and bottleneck features provide complementary semantic and structural conditions, RVQ visual side information further improves reconstruction quality, and layered unequal error protection helps improve recovery at low SNRs. Code-rate allocation experiments reveal a tradeoff between the reliability of fundamental conditions and visual-detail reconstruction under a limited visual-feature coding budget, providing guidance for allocating protection resources in underwater acoustic image transmission.
tldr: The paper proposes a generative image communication framework for underwater acoustic channels using cross-modal semantic successive refinement with text, bottleneck features, and RVQ-compressed visual side information.
motivation: Underwater acoustic communication has limited bandwidth and complex channel conditions, making efficient image transmission and reliable reconstruction difficult.
method: The transmitter sends text descriptions, compact bottleneck features, and RVQ-compressed visual side information; the receiver fuses text and bottleneck features for a base estimate, uses RVQ indices for residual correction, and reconstructs images with a one-step Pixel Mean Flow model, aided by CLIP-based semantic consistency and unequal error protection.
result: Simulations on COCO 2017 images and measured Watermark underwater acoustic channel records show that text and bottleneck features are complementary, RVQ side information improves reconstruction, and layered unequal error protection helps at low SNRs.
conclusion: The framework provides guidance for allocating protection resources in underwater acoustic image transmission, revealing a tradeoff between fundamental semantic reliability and visual-detail reconstruction under limited coding budget.

title: Gridshield: Verifiable Grid Feasibility And Manipulation Resistance In Privacy-Preserving Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading
authors: Abdullahil Kafi, Md Zahidul Islam, Alvi Ataur Khalil
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blockchain-based peer-to-peer (P2P) energy markets let neighbors trade directly, but concentrate unchecked power in the clearing operator. Most prior work addresses only part of this: network-aware clearing respects grid constraints but operates on plaintext allocations, while privacy-preserving designs hide bids yet either drop the network constraint, enforce it only inside an unauditable computation, or recover it at the cost of a per-circuit trusted setup. Neither considers what happens if an adversary captures the operator's clearing privilege to reorder trades for profit or curtail a rival. We present GRIDSHIELD, a P2P energy-trading system that clears sealed bids with an order-independent batch program, removing the welfare a compromised operator can extract by reordering trades, and proves the result grid-feasible via an aggregated congestion-feasibility proof (ACFP). Exploiting the additive homomorphism of Pedersen commitments, ACFP reconstructs each grid constraint directly from per-bus commitments, reducing feeder-wide feasibility verification over any public grid constraints to a single aggregated range proof over the hidden allocation, with a reveal-and-recompute challenge that catches feasible yet unfair clearings. We introduce congestion-responsibility fairness (CRF), a metric scoring curtailment against each party's physical responsibility for congestion rather than consumption. We evaluate GRIDSHIELD against three prior P2P energy-trading designs across four feeders, including a 240-node Midwest feeder with real hourly loads, on a live Hyperledger Fabric network benchmarked with Hyperledger Caliper. GRIDSHIELD proves an entire round feasible with a few-kilobyte proof and no trusted setup, rejects infeasible allocations two of the three compared designs accept, and sustains [MATH]1064 tx/s.
tldr: GRIDSHIELD is a blockchain-based peer-to-peer energy trading system using privacy-preserving sealed-bid clearing and aggregated congestion-feasibility proofs to prevent operator manipulation.
motivation: P2P energy markets concentrate power in clearing operators, and existing privacy-preserving designs either ignore grid constraints, rely on unauditable computation, or require trusted setup, while also leaving clearing operators able to manipulate trade ordering.
method: The system clears sealed bids with an order-independent batch program and proves grid feasibility via an aggregated congestion-feasibility proof over Pedersen commitments, together with a reveal-and-recompute challenge and a congestion-responsibility fairness metric.
result: GRIDSHIELD produces a few-kilobyte feasibility proof without trusted setup, rejects infeasible allocations accepted by two of three compared designs, and sustains about 1064 tx/s on Hyperledger Fabric.
conclusion: The paper advances practical privacy-preserving and manipulation-resistant P2P energy trading, but it is outside the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems research directions.

title: Exact Signal Recovery From Generative Priors With Sigmoid Output Activation
authors: Matthew S. Scott, Yaniv Plan, \"ozg\"ur Y{\i}lmaz
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show exact signal recovery in generative compressed sensing for feedforward neural networks with piecewise-linear activations and a final sigmoid activation, with no assumption of expansivity. Consider a ReLU network of depth [MATH] with a sigmoid final activation, whose input layer, of dimension [MATH], is the narrowest, and let [MATH] be the geometric mean of the widths of its layers. We show that, with high probability, all signals of the range whose entries lie in [MATH] are uniformly recovered from [MATH] measurements.
tldr: The paper proves exact signal recovery guarantees for generative compressed sensing using feedforward ReLU networks with a sigmoid output activation, without requiring expansivity.
motivation: Generative priors can outperform sparsity priors in compressed sensing, but existing recovery guarantees often rely on restrictive assumptions such as network expansivity; the authors aim to remove this requirement.
method: They analyze a depth-L ReLU network with a final sigmoid activation whose input layer is the narrowest, and derive uniform recovery guarantees from a number of measurements depending on the geometric mean of layer widths.
result: With high probability, all in-range signals with entries in a bounded interval are recovered exactly from a number of measurements scaling with the geometric mean of network widths.
conclusion: Sigmoid output activations enable provable compressed sensing with generative priors under mild architectural assumptions, broadening the applicability of generative recovery theory.

title: Variational Splines And Generalized Gaussian Processes
authors: Michael Unser
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tikhonov regularization, kriging, and Gaussian-process regression share the same algorithm because, for a linear inverse problem with a Gaussian prior and Gaussian noise, the minimum-mean-square-error (MMSE) estimator is the solution of a regularized least-squares problem. We show that this equivalence survives the passage from vectors to generalized functions: the regularized least-squares estimators become generalized splines, and the Gaussian random vectors become generalized Gaussian processes (GGPs) on the dual of a nuclear space. A whitening operator [MATH] specifies both the native Hilbert space [MATH] of the splines and a family of GGPs, which solve a stochastic differential equation subject to boundary conditions. We prove that the Gaussian spaces of these processes are congruent to the core [MATH] of the native space, and that their MMSE estimators from finitely many linear measurements are generalized splines. Our framework extends the classical correspondences of Kimeldorf-Wahba, Parzen and Kailath in two respects: our estimators form a broader class that includes generalized functions, and we give a proper Bayesian treatment of the case where the null space of [MATH] is non-trivial. The framework gives a precise meaning to statements such as ``fractional splines are the optimal estimators of fractional Brownian motion,'' and it provides a rigorous Bayesian formulation of infinite-dimensional linear inverse problems.
tldr: The paper proves that the classical equivalence between Tikhonov regularization, kriging, and Gaussian-process regression extends from finite-dimensional vectors to generalized functions, yielding generalized splines and generalized Gaussian processes on the dual of a nuclear space.
motivation: Tikhonov regularization, kriging and GP regression share the same estimator because the MMSE estimator under Gaussian prior and noise solves a regularized least-squares problem; the authors ask whether this equivalence survives the passage to generalized functions and infinite-dimensional inverse problems.
method: A whitening operator specifies a native Hilbert space of splines and a family of generalized Gaussian processes solving a stochastic differential equation with boundary conditions; the Gaussian spaces are shown to be congruent to the core of the native space.
result: MMSE estimators from finitely many linear measurements are shown to be generalized splines, extending the Kimeldorf-Wahba, Parzen and Kailath correspondences to generalized functions and giving a proper Bayesian treatment of non-trivial null spaces.
conclusion: The framework rigorously grounds statements such as 'fractional splines are optimal estimators of fractional Brownian motion' and provides a Bayesian formulation of infinite-dimensional linear inverse problems.

title: NN-Based FeFET Compact Modeling For Spice Simulation
authors: Rodion Novkin, Simon Thomann, Hussam Amrouch
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prototyping and early-stage circuit evaluation for emerging transistor technologies require fast and accurate compact models for SPICE simulations. Standard physics-based compact models, such as BSIM, offer high fidelity but demand extensive domain expertise and time-consuming equation formulation for every new physical effect, significantly slowing technology development. Neural network (NN)-based models offer a scalable alternative approach, but they rely heavily on smooth numerical solver data with explicit high-order derivative information. However, measurement data suffers from complex noise patterns, making derivative extraction challenging and complicating NN-based transistor modeling. This work presents a derivative-free NN training framework employing spectral normalization to naturally smooth derivative behavior and filter measurement noise. Using drain current measurements from a fabricated 28 nm ferroelectric device, we design an NN-based compact model that captures the full spectrum of polarization amplitudes and supports dynamic polarization switching in transient simulations. To demonstrate its capability, we deploy the model in a commercial SPICE software to simulate write and read operations for large-scale memory arrays with up to 512x512 size, including parasitic effects. Our approach bridges raw measurements with NN-based SPICE-compatible transistor modeling, significantly reducing model development time and enabling rapid circuit-level prototyping for emerging devices.
tldr: The authors develop a derivative-free neural-network compact model for 28 nm ferroelectric FETs that is smooth enough for SPICE circuit simulation.
motivation: Emerging transistor technologies need fast, accurate compact models for early circuit prototyping, but physics-based models like BSIM require extensive manual equation derivation and NN-based models struggle with noisy measurement data and derivative extraction.
method: They train a neural network with spectral normalization to smooth derivative behavior and filter measurement noise, fitting drain current measurements from a fabricated 28 nm FeFET and capturing the full range of polarization amplitudes including dynamic switching.
result: The model is deployed in commercial SPICE software to simulate write and read operations of memory arrays up to 512x512, including parasitic effects, without requiring derivative data.
conclusion: The framework bridges raw noisy measurements to SPICE-compatible NN transistor models, cutting model development time and enabling rapid circuit-level prototyping of emerging devices.

title: Exhaustive Search Is Hard To Beat In Constant Depth For Hyperclique And Orthogonal Vectors
authors: Nikolai Chukhin
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A hyperclique in an [MATH]-uniform hypergraph is a set of vertices in which every [MATH]-subset is an edge. A simple exhaustive search algorithm detects a hyperclique on [MATH] vertices in an [MATH]-uniform hypergraph on [MATH] vertices by checking all [MATH] sets of [MATH] vertices. This algorithm can be expressed as a depth-two circuit with at most [MATH] gates and wires. For hypercliques of *constant* size, Amano (2010) showed that this circuit is almost optimal: for large [MATH], constant-depth circuits need [MATH] wires. We prove that this circuit remains hard to beat even for hypercliques of *polynomial* size. More precisely, circuits of depth [MATH] need [MATH] gates for [MATH], and [MATH] gates for [MATH] that tends to infinity. Our hyperclique bound and the method behind it also lead to lower bounds for two central problems of fine-grained complexity. First, we extend the bound [MATH] of Rossman (2008) for [MATH]-Clique from cliques of *constant* size to cliques of *polynomial* size: circuits of depth [MATH] detecting a clique on [MATH] vertices in an [MATH]-vertex graph need [MATH] gates for [MATH]. Second, a reduction of Choudhury, Limaye, Sreenivasaiah, and Srinivasan (2026) turns our hyperclique bound into a lower bound of [MATH] gates for [MATH]-Orthogonal Vectors ([MATH]-OV) at every fixed depth for vectors of dimension [MATH]; this proves the [MATH]-OV Conjecture for constant-depth circuits in polylogarithmic dimension. Finally, for [MATH]-OV in logarithmic dimension, we give a simple proof that depth-three circuits need [MATH] wires, which answers a question of Kane and Williams (2019).
tldr: The paper proves constant-depth circuit lower bounds for hyperclique detection and related fine-grained complexity problems including Orthogonal Vectors.
motivation: It aims to extend known circuit lower bounds from constant-size hypercliques and cliques to polynomial-size instances, addressing central conjectures in fine-grained complexity.
method: The author analyzes bounded-depth circuits with gates and wires, proving lower bounds via hyperclique reductions to clique and Orthogonal Vectors problems.
result: Depth-d circuits require superpolynomial gates for polynomial-size hypercliques and cliques under stated parameter regimes, yielding lower bounds for constant-depth Orthogonal Vectors and resolving a question of Kane and Williams for logarithmic dimension.
conclusion: Exhaustive search is essentially optimal for these problems in constant depth, with implications for fine-grained complexity conjectures.

title: Optimal Marginal Mixing For Transvection-Based Trapdoored Matrices Over Large Fields
authors: Mark Braverman, Aayush Jain, Stephen Newman
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: are pseudorandom matrices admitting a fast matrix-vector multiplication algorithm given the secret key. We study a candidate family of such matrices: matrices generated by short random on \(_n(_q)\), whose steps are given by adding a random multiple of a random row of the current state to another. We show that the worst-case time for any nonempty set \(\subseteq [n]\times[n]\) of matrix entries to come within TV distance \(\varepsilon\leq {4}\) of its stationary marginal under this walk is \(\Theta(||+n\log(n/\varepsilon))\), uniformly over all \(\) and \(q\geq Q_(n)\). This is asymptotically optimal, and resolves open questions about the mixing times of transvection walks. We derive concrete upper and lower bounds for \(n\geq 256\). Surprisingly, our bounds also hold conditioned on the row-pair structure of the walk, except on a fraction at most \(\varepsilon\) of such structures. This implies that these walks may be pseudorandom even after conditioning on the row-pair structure, and therefore that trapdoored matrices built with these walks may be universal. Assuming the conjectured structure-conditioned pseudorandomness of short walks, we exhibit highly efficient, highly parallelizable, and universal trapdoored matrices over \(_n(_q)\), \(_n(_q)\), and \(_q^{n\times n}\). The families over \(_n(_q)\) and \(_n(_q)\) admit equally efficient trapdoors for their inverses, making them the first to do so for finite-field trapdoored matrices. We discuss attacks, analyzing one in detail, and lay out directions for further investigation.
tldr: The paper analyzes mixing times of transvection-based random walks over finite fields and uses them to construct trapdoored pseudorandom matrices with fast matrix-vector multiplication.
motivation: Trapdoored pseudorandom matrices can enable cryptographic obfuscation-like primitives, but efficient and universal constructions over large finite fields are challenging.
method: The authors study a random walk on matrices generated by adding random multiples of random rows to other rows, and prove sharp bounds on the time for marginal distributions of matrix entries to mix in total variation distance.
result: They establish asymptotically optimal mixing time bounds of order Θ(|| + n log(n/ε)) uniformly over entry sets and large fields, and derive concrete bounds for n ≥ 256, including conditioning on row-pair structure.
conclusion: Under a conjectured structure-conditioned pseudorandomness assumption, the walks yield efficient universal trapdoored matrices over several matrix rings and fields, with efficient inverse trapdoors for two families.

title: Representation Theory And Massive Spectral Zeta Functions On Spherical Space Forms
authors: Victoria Martin, Allan Merino, Rahul Poddar, Simon Roby
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the spectral theory of the massive scalar kinetic operator on spherical space forms [MATH], where [MATH] is a finite subgroup of [MATH] acting freely on [MATH]. Using the Peter-Weyl theorem and Molien series we compute the spectrum of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on [MATH] directly from representation theory, obtaining the eigenvalues and their multiplicities for all lens spaces [MATH] and for each ADE-class of finite subgroups of [MATH], which includes homogeneous lens spaces, prism spaces and quotients by the binary tetrahedral, octahedral and icosahedral groups, the last also known as the Poincar\'e homology sphere. For homogeneous quotients by subgroups of even order, we construct the meromorphic continuation of the spectral zeta function of the massive kinetic operator and obtain the general zeta-regularized determinant in closed form. The determinant is expressed as a finite sum of polylogarithms, valid for all real mass, and depends on [MATH] only through its order and a finite set of parameters which we call twist coefficients fixed by the dimensions of the [MATH]-invariant subspaces. As a complementary approach, we express the heat trace of the kinetic operator on spherical space forms in terms of Jacobi theta functions, whose modular properties relate the spectral zeta function to geometric data, the volume and closed geodesic lengths of [MATH]. We find that the spectral zeta function admits a rapidly convergent expansion in the heavy mass sector in terms of modified Bessel functions, and provides an independent check on the determinant. This framework extends to quotients of higher-dimensional manifolds directly, which we outline for future work.
tldr: The paper computes spectra and massive spectral zeta functions on spherical space forms using representation theory and Molien series.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize the Laplace-Beltrami spectrum and zeta-regularized determinants on quotients of spheres by finite groups.
method: They use the Peter-Weyl theorem and Molien series to obtain eigenvalues and multiplicities, then construct meromorphic continuations and heat-trace expressions via Jacobi theta functions.
result: Closed-form determinants are expressed as finite sums of polylogarithms, with heavy-mass expansions in modified Bessel functions and geometric interpretations via volume and closed geodesic lengths.
conclusion: The framework provides a representation-theoretic approach to spectral zeta functions on spherical space forms and is outlined for higher-dimensional quotients.

title: Mueller Matrix Decomposition For A General Rotating Compensator Ellipsometer
authors: Aaron Chew, Purnima P. Balakrishnan, Bryan M. Barnes, John H. Burnett, Colton K. Dudley, Steven E. Grantham, Stephanie L. Moffitt, Charles Tarrio, Thomas A. Germer
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work develops a Mueller matrix decomposition that factors a nondepolarizing Mueller matrix [MATH] into three components [MATH], where the elements [MATH], which correspond to a diagonal Jones matrix, are separated from rotations and circular diattenuation [MATH]. This decomposition is employed to calibrate a prototype reflective rotating-compensator ellipsometer designed to operate using extreme ultraviolet (EUV) radiation. This decomposition allows for the measurement of the full Mueller matrix of a sample without full knowledge of the compensators or the source polarization, while allowing for significant diattenuation and retardance for the optics. A generalization of the decomposition is developed for depolarizing Mueller matrices, and the technique is tested on reflection data collected on an Au mirror at [MATH] nm.
tldr: The paper develops a Mueller matrix decomposition that separates a diagonal Jones-matrix-like component from rotations and circular diattenuation, and uses it to calibrate a prototype extreme-ultraviolet rotating-compensator ellipsometer.
motivation: Full Mueller matrix measurement typically requires complete knowledge of compensator and source polarization properties; the authors seek a calibration scheme that relaxes these requirements while tolerating large diattenuation and retardance in the optics.
method: A nondepolarizing Mueller matrix is factored into three components isolating a diagonal Jones-type part from rotation and circular diattenuation contributions, with an extension to depolarizing matrices, and the technique is applied to calibrate a reflective rotating-compensator ellipsometer and tested on an Au mirror at EUV wavelengths.
result: The decomposition enables measurement of a sample's full Mueller matrix without full prior knowledge of the compensators or source polarization, and the approach is validated against reflection data from an Au mirror.
conclusion: The proposed decomposition provides a practical calibration route for EUV ellipsometry and generalizes to depolarizing samples, though it lies entirely in classical optical metrology.

title: Stroh--Hamiltonian Framework For Modeling Incompressible Poroelastic Materials
authors: Vincenzo Tibullo Kinza Arshad
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Stroh sextic formalism, developed by Stroh, offers a compelling framework for representing the equilibrium equations in anisotropic elasticity. This approach has proven particularly effective for studying multilayered structures and time-harmonic problems, owing to its ability to seamlessly integrate physical constraints into the analysis. By recognizing that the Stroh formalism aligns with the canonical Hamiltonian structure, this work extends its application to Biot's poroelasticity, focusing on scenarios where the solid material is incompressible and there is no fluid pressure gradient. The study introduces a novel Hamiltonian-based approach to analyze such systems, offering deeper insights into the interplay between solid incompressibility and fluid-solid coupling. A key novelty lies in the derivation of canonical equations under these constraints, enabling clearer interpretations of reversible poroelastic behavior. However, the framework assumes perfectly drained conditions and neglects dissipative effects, which limits its applicability to fully realistic scenarios involving energy loss or complex fluid dynamics. Despite this limitation, the work provides a foundational step toward understanding constrained poroelastic systems and paves the way for future extensions to more general cases, including dissipative and nonlinear regimes.
tldr: The paper extends the Stroh sextic formalism and Hamiltonian framework to incompressible poroelastic materials under drained, non-dissipative conditions.
motivation: Stroh's formalism is effective for anisotropic elasticity and multilayered time-harmonic problems, and the authors aim to extend its canonical Hamiltonian structure to Biot poroelasticity with solid incompressibility and no fluid pressure gradient.
method: The authors formulate the equilibrium equations of incompressible poroelasticity within a Hamiltonian framework, deriving canonical equations under the stated constraints.
result: The framework yields canonical equations that clarify reversible poroelastic behavior and the coupling between solid incompressibility and fluid-solid interaction, though it neglects dissipation and assumes perfectly drained conditions.
conclusion: This is a foundational step toward Hamiltonian modeling of constrained poroelastic systems, with future work needed to include dissipative and nonlinear regimes.

title: Construction, Enumeration And Duality Of Perfectly Balanced Musical Sets Of Order $2pq$
authors: Paul Lascabettes, Sidney Ali, Alexandre Popoff, Moreno Andreatta
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a comprehensive study of perfectly balanced musical sets, also known in the literature as vanishing sums of roots of unity, in the particular case of order [MATH]. Starting from the well-established result concerning the decomposition of such sets as an integer linear combination of regular polygons, we first provide an algebraic formalization that allows to explicitly construct all these sets. We then propose six different decompositions of each set into regular polygons. Moreover, by investigating their combinatorial enumeration, we derive a formula for the exact number of these sets for a given order [MATH], and describe their distribution and cardinality for the particular case of order [MATH]. One of the main results concerns the duality that can be established between these sets. In particular, we prove that every non-periodic minimal perfectly balanced set of order [MATH] can be combined with another one to produce a self-complementary [MATH]-periodic set, and the reciprocal also holds. Finally, we demonstrate that the modulus of the discrete Fourier transform coefficients of dual sets are related. All these results shed new light on the distribution of perfectly balanced sets of order [MATH] and suggest new mathematical questions in a more general case.
tags: vanishing sums of roots of unity
tldr: A mathematical music-theory study of perfectly balanced musical sets (vanishing sums of roots of unity) of order 2pq, giving explicit constructions, six polygon decompositions, an exact enumeration formula, and a duality relating non-periodic minimal sets to self-complementary periodic ones.
motivation: Perfectly balanced sets, equivalently vanishing sums of roots of unity, are of interest both in algebraic number theory and in scale/pitch-class theory in mathematical musicology; the order 2pq case lacked a systematic construction and counting theory.
method: Building on the known decomposition of such sets into integer linear combinations of regular polygons, the authors develop an algebraic formalism to construct all sets, propose six distinct polygon decompositions, and carry out a combinatorial enumeration; they also analyze discrete Fourier transform coefficients of dual sets.
result: They obtain an exact counting formula for the number of such sets at a given order, describe the distribution and cardinalities for order 2pq, and prove a duality: every non-periodic minimal perfectly balanced set pairs with another to form a self-complementary p-periodic set, and conversely, with the moduli of DFT coefficients of dual sets related.
conclusion: The work clarifies the structure and distribution of perfectly balanced sets of order 2pq and points toward open questions in the general case; it is a pure mathematics/music-theory contribution with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
keywords: vanishing sums of roots of unity

title: On Parallel Sums Of Set-Valued Operators: Monotonicity, Paramonotonicity, And Decomposition Invariance
authors: Salihah Thabet Alwadani
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate structural properties of the parallel sum of set-valued operators in a real Hilbert space, with particular emphasis on monotonicity, maximal monotonicity, and paramonotonicity. We examine the decomposition-invariance property of the parallel sum of two paramonotone operators and provide a direct proof based on monotonicity and the equality of admissible decompositions. This approach establishes the required orthogonality relations without invoking the Attouch--Th{\'e}ra Duality duality framework. We also revisit the classical maximal-monotonicity property of the parallel sum and present an alternative graph-based derivation involving an auxiliary shifted operator. Furthermore, we study the parallel sum of a set-valued operator and the normal cone operator associated with a closed linear subspace. Explicit characterizations of its values, domain, and range are presented, and a decomposition-independent representation is obtained under paramonotonicity through the orthogonality of the underlying subspaces. These results provide a unified and self-contained treatment of selected properties of parallel sums and clarify the role of paramonotonicity in their structural behavior.
tldr: A purely mathematical study of parallel sums of set-valued monotone operators in real Hilbert spaces, covering monotonicity, maximal monotonicity, paramonotonicity, and decomposition invariance.
motivation: The parallel sum is a classical construction in convex analysis and monotone operator theory, and the authors aim to give a unified, self-contained treatment of its structural properties without relying on the Attouch–Théra duality framework.
method: Direct operator-theoretic arguments based on monotonicity and equality of admissible decompositions establish the required orthogonality relations, complemented by an alternative graph-based derivation using an auxiliary shifted operator; the parallel sum with a normal cone operator for a closed subspace is characterized explicitly.
result: The paper proves decomposition invariance for parallel sums of two paramonotone operators, re-derives maximal monotonicity via a graph-based approach, and provides explicit characterizations of values, domain, and range for the operator–normal-cone parallel sum, including a decomposition-independent representation.
conclusion: The results clarify the role of paramonotonicity in the structure of parallel sums and consolidate known properties into a unified framework.

title: Tight Lower Bounds Under Matched High-Order H\"older Smoothness And Uniform Convexity
authors: Cedar Site Bai
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we provide tight lower bounds for minimizing high-order H\"older-smooth and uniformly convex functions when their orders match. Specifically, we consider functions whose [MATH]-order derivatives are H\"older continuous with degree [MATH] and parameter [MATH], and that are uniformly convex with degree [MATH] and parameter [MATH]. When these orders match, namely, [MATH], we show that any deterministic algorithm with access to derivatives up to order [MATH] requires [MATH] oracle calls to reduce an initial optimality gap of [MATH] to [MATH]. This matches the corresponding upper bound and establishes a higher-order uniformly convex counterpart to Nesterov's classical first-order lower bound for strongly convex functions. Rather than directly generalizing Nesterov's classical quadratic-chain construction, we develop a multiscale phase-wise construction that preserves previous oracle responses while maintaining global H\"older smoothness and uniform convexity. Our result resolves the matched case left open by existing lower bounds for the two asymmetric regimes.
tldr: The paper establishes tight oracle-complexity lower bounds for deterministic algorithms minimizing functions that are simultaneously high-order Hölder smooth and uniformly convex when the smoothness and convexity orders match.
motivation: Existing lower bounds cover only the two asymmetric regimes where the Hölder smoothness order and the uniform convexity order differ, leaving the matched case open; this work closes that gap.
method: Instead of generalizing Nesterov's quadratic-chain construction, the author builds a multiscale, phase-wise adversarial function construction that preserves earlier oracle responses while maintaining global high-order Hölder smoothness and uniform convexity.
result: Any deterministic algorithm with access to derivatives up to order p requires a number of oracle calls matching the known upper bound to shrink the initial optimality gap, yielding a higher-order analogue of Nesterov's first-order strongly convex lower bound.
conclusion: The matched-order case is resolved, completing the picture of complexity lower bounds for high-order Hölder-smooth uniformly convex optimization and matching existing upper bounds.

title: IC-rigidity And Generalizations Of A Theorem Of Mahler
authors: Scott Schmieding Bryna Kra
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mahler showed that for every irrational [MATH] and every base [MATH], there is a single positive integer [MATH] such that every digit in [MATH] occurs infinitely often in the base-[MATH] expansion of [MATH]. Furstenberg later observed that dynamical methods can be used to give a different proof. Building on this perspective, we give generalizations of Mahler's theorem in two directions: the multipliers are a syndetic subset of certain multiplicative semigroups, and analogous versions hold in higher dimensions. Our main tool is IC-rigidity, a type of rigidity which is a hybrid of topological and measurable constraints.
tldr: The paper generalizes Mahler's theorem on digit occurrences in irrational base expansions using a hybrid topological-measurable rigidity notion called IC-rigidity.
motivation: Mahler proved that every irrational has a multiplier such that all digits occur infinitely often in its base expansion, and Furstenberg observed a dynamical proof; this work extends that perspective to syndetic multiplier sets and higher dimensions.
method: The authors introduce IC-rigidity, a rigidity condition combining topological and measurable constraints, and use it to prove generalized digit-frequency results for multiplicative semigroups and multidimensional analogues.
result: They obtain generalizations of Mahler's theorem where multipliers form a syndetic subset of certain multiplicative semigroups, and establish analogous higher-dimensional statements.
conclusion: IC-rigidity provides a unified framework for extending Mahler-type digit-distribution theorems beyond the classical one-dimensional setting.

title: Linear Cotype Bounds For Nonlinear Spectral Gaps Of Scalar Expanders
authors: Achintya Raya Polavarapu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a finite simple [MATH]-regular graph, [MATH], whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue satisfies [MATH], where [MATH]. We prove that the Poincar\'e constant satisfies $[MATH][MATH]X[MATH]K[MATH]q[MATH]C[MATH]O(qC/\delta)[MATH]n[MATH]C,K[MATH]q[MATH]\log n[MATH]\ell_q^n$.
tldr: The paper proves linear cotype bounds relating nonlinear spectral gaps and Poincare constants for scalar expanders on regular graphs.
motivation: It addresses spectral gap and Poincare constant bounds in expander graphs, a topic in pure mathematics and spectral graph theory.
method: The authors use analytic and graph-theoretic techniques to derive inequalities involving the second adjacency eigenvalue and Poincare constants.
result: They establish a linear cotype bound of the form O(qC/δ) for the Poincare constant under a spectral gap condition on the graph.
conclusion: The work contributes to nonlinear spectral graph theory but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Near-Optimal Complexity Of Finding Approximate Local Minima Of Nonconvex Finite Sums
authors: Qihao Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the component-oracle complexity of finding approximate local minima of nonconvex finite sums under mean-squared averaged smoothness with parameter [MATH] and a [MATH]-Lipschitz average Hessian. Each query returns the value, gradient, and one Hessian-vector product of a component. We show that the complexity in the high-accuracy regime [MATH] is [MATH] for a sufficiently large initial gap [MATH]. We attain the upper bound by adapting the inverse solver and eigenvector routine of FastCubic to averaged smoothness. Our lower bound assigns the bridge edges of a nested chain to random components; a replicated spectral construction gives the same bound for unrestricted randomized algorithms. Under individual smoothness, a factor of [MATH] remains for [MATH], up to logarithmic factors. In the complementary low-accuracy regime, we propose PathVR, which uses [MATH] queries and matches a lower bound from dense weak hiding.
tldr: The paper establishes near-optimal component-oracle complexity bounds for finding approximate local minima of nonconvex finite-sum optimization problems under averaged smoothness assumptions.
motivation: Nonconvex finite-sum optimization underlies much of modern machine learning, but tight oracle-complexity characterizations of finding approximate local minima, especially with Hessian-vector product access, remained incomplete.
method: The authors adapt the inverse solver and eigenvector routine of FastCubic to mean-squared averaged smoothness, and prove lower bounds via a nested-chain construction assigning bridge edges to random components, with a replicated spectral construction for randomized algorithms; they also propose PathVR for the low-accuracy regime.
result: They obtain matching upper and lower complexity bounds in the high-accuracy regime for sufficiently large initial gap, leave only a logarithmic-factor gap under individual smoothness, and show PathVR matches a dense weak-hiding lower bound in the low-accuracy regime.
conclusion: The work nearly closes the complexity gap for finding approximate local minima in nonconvex finite sums, though it is a purely classical optimization result with no quantum information, thermodynamic, or networking content.

title: The Invocation Bottleneck In LLM-Based Lossless Compression: What Can Be Removed And What Must Be Traded
authors: Zhe Yan, Yihao Liu, Antonio Boffa, Huanchen Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) compress text far better than classical compressors, but LLM-based compressors are slow, particularly during decompression. We argue that their decoding time has two fundamentally different sources. Execution redundancy, such as per-token host transfers, CPU-side coding, and token-by-token encoding, is work that the coded output does not require and can be removed without changing a single output bit. Sequential dependency, one model call per decoded token, is inherent to lossless decoding and cannot be removed by better execution, only traded for more calls or for more bits. We remove execution redundancy with a GPU-resident pipeline whose block-parallel encoding is made lossless in half precision by batch-invariant kernels, speeding up arithmetic coding by up to 5.8x in encoding and 3.0x in decoding without changing its compression rate. We then study the two ways of trading sequential dependency, speculative dual-model coding (SDMC) and multi-token single-model coding (MSMC), characterize the compression cost of predicting several tokens from a shared prefix, and identify the workloads in which fewer model calls are worth that cost.
tldr: The paper analyzes the decompression bottleneck of LLM-based lossless compression, separating removable 'execution redundancy' from inherent 'sequential dependency', and proposes a GPU-resident batch-invariant pipeline plus two strategies (SDMC and MSMC) for trading sequential dependence against compression cost.
motivation: LLM-based compressors achieve better compression than classical tools but are slow, especially in decompression, and the sources of this slowness have not been cleanly separated.
method: The authors partition decoding cost into execution redundancy (per-token host transfers, CPU-side coding, token-by-token encoding) and sequential dependency (one model call per token). They build a GPU-resident, block-parallel arithmetic-coding pipeline made lossless in half precision via batch-invariant kernels, then evaluate speculative dual-model coding (SDMC) and multi-token single-model coding (MSMC).
result: Removing execution redundancy speeds arithmetic coding up to 5.8x for encoding and 3.0x for decoding with bit-identical output; the two trade strategies are characterized in terms of the compression cost of predicting multiple tokens from a shared prefix, indicating which workloads benefit from fewer model calls.
conclusion: Execution redundancy can be eliminated outright, whereas sequential dependency in lossless LLM decoding can only be traded for more model calls or more bits; the paper identifies when such trades are worthwhile.

title: Weak And Strong Convergence Of A General Splitting Approach For Monotone Multioperator Inclusions
authors: Minh N. Dao, Matthew K. Tam, Thang D. Truong
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study a general forward-backward splitting approach for monotone inclusion problems that simultaneously accommodate set-valued, monotone Lipschitz continuous, and cocoercive operators. Weak convergence is established under a general setting. Strong convergence is obtained when both the maximally monotone operators are linear relations and the monotone Lipschitz continuous and cocoercive operators are linear. When the set-valued operators are normal cones to closed linear subspaces, we derive an explicit characterization of limit points of generated sequences using a new technique. Numerical experiments on a quadratic minimization problem with multiple-set split feasibility constraints are presented to illustrate the theoretical results.
tldr: The paper develops a general forward-backward splitting method for monotone multioperator inclusion problems, establishing weak convergence generally and strong convergence for linear-relation/linear-operator cases.
motivation: Monotone inclusion problems involving mixed set-valued, Lipschitz, and cocoercive operators arise in optimization, but unified splitting schemes with both weak and strong convergence guarantees are lacking.
method: A forward-backward splitting algorithm is proposed for sum-structured monotone inclusions, analyzed via weak convergence arguments, with strong convergence derived when maximally monotone operators are linear relations and Lipschitz/cocoercive operators are linear.
result: Weak convergence is proved in a general setting, strong convergence under linearity assumptions, and an explicit characterization of limit points is obtained for normal-cone (closed linear subspace) operators; numerical experiments on split feasibility quadratic minimization illustrate the theory.
conclusion: The framework provides a unified convergence theory for splitting methods on composite monotone inclusions, though its scope is purely mathematical optimization.

title: Descriptor Representations Of Geometric port-Hamiltonian Systems On Hilbert Spaces
authors: Timo Reis Anna Fischer
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish conversions in both directions between geometric and descriptor representations of linear port-Hamiltonian systems on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. For the geometric-to-descriptor conversion, we represent the possibly multivalued inverse Dirac relation by a skew-adjoint operator on enlarged Hilbert spaces, retaining the original operator-domain restrictions. The construction accommodates internal and external ports. We show that the conversions preserve trajectories and the power balance. An incompressible Kelvin--Voigt solid illustrates the results.
tldr: The paper develops conversions between geometric and descriptor representations of linear port-Hamiltonian systems on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
motivation: Port-Hamiltonian systems provide an energy-based framework for modeling interconnected dynamical systems, and different representations are useful for analysis and control.
method: The authors construct bidirectional conversions by representing the possibly multivalued inverse Dirac relation via a skew-adjoint operator on enlarged Hilbert spaces while preserving operator-domain restrictions.
result: They show that the conversions preserve trajectories and the power balance, and illustrate the results with an incompressible Kelvin–Voigt solid.
conclusion: The work extends port-Hamiltonian systems theory on Hilbert spaces by establishing equivalence between geometric and descriptor formulations.

title: $C_2$-Cofiniteness Of Permutation Orbifolds I: Relative $c_1$ Descent
authors: Jiancai Sun Yuhan Gu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06201v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a relative [MATH]-cofiniteness criterion for [MATH]-cofiniteness of finite group orbifolds. For permutation actions on a simple, self contragredient, [MATH]-cofinite vertex operator algebra of CFT type, it suffices to check a single relation for a derivative of the conformal vector in the Virasoro vertex operator algebra. This reduces the problem to a calculation depending only on the central charge and tensor degree. An exact calculation then proves cofiniteness for a family of nonsolvable permutation orbifolds without restricting the central charge.
tldr: The paper proves a relative C_2-cofiniteness criterion for finite group permutation orbifolds of vertex operator algebras, reducing the problem to a central-charge- and tensor-degree-dependent calculation.
motivation: C_2-cofiniteness is important in vertex operator algebra theory and conformal field theory, and the authors aim to establish criteria for finite group orbifolds, particularly permutation orbifolds.
method: They derive a relative C_2-cofiniteness descent criterion and show that, for permutation actions on simple self-contragredient C_2-cofinite vertex operator algebras of CFT type, it suffices to verify one relation involving a derivative of the conformal vector in the Virasoro vertex operator algebra.
result: This reduces the verification to a calculation depending only on the central charge and tensor degree, and an exact calculation proves C_2-cofiniteness for a family of nonsolvable permutation orbifolds without central-charge restrictions.
conclusion: The work provides a new algebraic criterion and explicit cofiniteness results for permutation orbifolds, contributing to vertex operator algebra and conformal field theory mathematics.

title: Learning Vs. Optimizing Players In Budgeted Games
authors: Giannis Fikioris, Balasubramanian Sivan, \'eva Tardos
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study repeated general games over [MATH] rounds between a utility-maximizing optimizer and a learning agent, where budget constraints couple the players' decisions across rounds. Without budgets, low swap regret simultaneously guarantees the learner sublinear regret and caps the optimizer at its Stackelberg value. Budgets break this picture: adversarial no-regret becomes impossible, so the natural goals are non-manipulability---no adaptive optimizer earns more than [MATH], where [MATH] is its Budgeted Stackelberg Equilibrium value---and low stochastic regret when the optimizer plays a fixed mixed strategy. We give an efficient, budget-feasible learning algorithm that achieves both goals in every budgeted game: any adaptive optimizer, budgeted or not, earns at most [MATH] in expectation, and if the optimizer plays a fixed mixed strategy on each of a constant number of intervals, the learner has [MATH] regret on each such interval. Our learner best responds to forecasts of the optimizer's play that are calibrated in two novel senses, since under budgets the calibration that prevents manipulation no longer yields low stochastic regret. Response calibration, which conditions on the learner's own mixed response by embedding its continuous mixing weight as a step function in [MATH], prevents manipulation without discretizing responses; dual-weighted Lagrangian calibration ensures low regret. Although low calibration error requires randomized forecasts---distributions over a continuous space that need not have a succinct representation or be directly computable---we construct such forecasts in polynomial time by simulating online gradient ascent.
tldr: The paper studies repeated budgeted general games between an optimizer and a learning agent, designing an efficient learner that prevents manipulation and achieves low stochastic regret via novel calibration methods.
motivation: Budget constraints break standard no-regret guarantees and make adversarial no-regret impossible, so the authors seek alternative guarantees: non-manipulability and low stochastic regret against fixed mixed strategies.
method: They introduce a budget-feasible learning algorithm using response calibration, dual-weighted Lagrangian calibration, and polynomial-time construction of randomized calibrated forecasts via simulated online gradient ascent.
result: The learner ensures any adaptive optimizer earns at most the Budgeted Stackelberg Equilibrium value and achieves low stochastic regret on intervals where the optimizer plays a fixed mixed strategy.
conclusion: The work provides efficient learning in budgeted repeated games with strong non-manipulability and regret guarantees, extending calibration and online learning techniques to budget-constrained settings.

title: CoordX Protocol: Peer To Peer Cryptographically Verified Shared Records
authors: Rob Ewin David Hyland-Wood
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: People, companies and software agents often must work on shared records even when they do not trust each other. Today they usually give those records to a central server. The server keeps the canonical copy, authenticates users, and decides who has permissions to act on the record. The CoordX Protocol removes the need for that central server. In the CoordX protocol the author of a record holds full permission over it. Permission for any other party to create, read or update the record is assigned by explicit grants and keys. An invitation only starts contact between two parties. It gives no permission. Each record is a causal tree of signed entries, and each entry is immutable. Each entry names the permission that allowed it. Any party can get the proof of that permission and check it without help from anyone. Two honest parties that check the same bytes, with the same keys and local settings, always get the same answer. The content is encrypted, so the relays that may carry it in transit see only sealed bytes. To exclude a party from future content, the other parties move to new keys. The protocol does not choose a winning version, does not put entries in time order, and does not need global agreement. Applications decide what the entries mean above the level of the protocol.
tldr: CoordX is a serverless peer-to-peer protocol in which each shared record is an immutable causal tree of signed, permission-tagged entries that any party can independently verify.
motivation: Mutually distrusting parties currently rely on a central server to hold the canonical copy of shared records, authenticate users, and enforce permissions, which creates a single point of trust and control.
method: The protocol replaces the server with explicit key-based permission grants, encrypted content distributed through untrusted relays, and per-record causal trees of signed entries where each entry cites the grant that authorized it and carries a self-contained verifiable proof.
result: Verification is deterministic across honest parties checking identical bytes, keys and local settings; exclusion of a party is achieved by key rotation, and the protocol deliberately avoids total ordering, conflict resolution, or global agreement.
conclusion: CoordX provides a cryptographically verifiable, decentralized alternative to central-server record management, leaving semantic interpretation of entries to higher-level applications.

title: Offline Learning Of Reserve Prices From Censored Bids
authors: Lavanya Marla, Yunzong Xu, Boxuan Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how a seller can learn a reserve price for a second-price auction from censored historical bid data. Because values below past reserves are unobserved, even unlimited data may not reveal which reserve earns the most revenue. Under a monotone hazard rate (MHR) assumption, we characterize exactly when an optimal reserve is identified, even though the value distribution may not be: either revenue has not yet begun to fall at the lowest historical reserve, so the best reserve lies among the observed bids, or the censored fraction is as large as MHR allows, which pins down the entire distribution. When identification fails, we derive the reserve that minimizes worst-case revenue regret over distributions consistent with the data, and prove that this unique minimax reserve and its regret depend on just two observable quantities: the censored fraction and the hazard just above the lowest historical reserve. With [MATH] historical bidders, the optimal reserve is learned with expected worst-case regret [MATH] when it lies among the observed bids, and [MATH] from the censored count alone when the censored fraction is as large as MHR allows and the optimum lies at or below the lowest reserve. In the nonidentifiable regime, plugging estimates of the two quantities into the minimax reserve gives expected worst-case regret within [MATH] of the population minimum under local density smoothness, with a matching minimax lower bound on a smooth class. Beyond MHR, we solve the minimax problem for regular and unrestricted distributions and prove an [MATH] learning bound in the regular nonidentifiable regime, given known bounds on the boundary parameters. Experiments on synthetic and eBay data show gains from exploiting MHR and the benefits of the robust rule when parametric models are misspecified.
tldr: The paper studies offline learning of revenue-optimal reserve prices in second-price auctions from censored bid data.
motivation: Sellers observing only bids above past reserve prices face censoring, so even abundant data may not identify the revenue-maximizing reserve.
method: Under monotone hazard rate assumptions, the authors characterize identification, derive minimax reserve rules for nonidentified regimes, and prove regret bounds; they also extend the analysis to regular and unrestricted distributions.
result: They show the minimax reserve depends on only the censored fraction and the hazard just above the lowest historical reserve, with matching minimax lower bounds and experiments on synthetic and eBay data.
conclusion: Exploiting MHR structure and robust minimax rules can improve reserve-price learning under censored bids and model misspecification.

title: Breaking The One-Player Extension Barrier: History-Aware Repair For Multiplayer Approximate Nash Equilibria
authors: Jinqi Tang, Shihong Ding, Cong Fang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computation of Nash equilibria is a central problem in algorithmic game theory, yet exact equilibrium computation is [MATH]-complete even for two-player games. This hardness motivates the study of polynomial-time algorithms for approximate Nash equilibria. While substantial progress has been made for two-player and three-player games, existing algorithms for general [MATH]-player games have largely relied on repeatedly applying one-player extension starting from improved fixed-player algorithms. Such improvements can at best strengthen the classical [MATH] guarantee to [MATH], for some constant [MATH] independent of [MATH]. We break this long-standing barrier by developing an iterative algorithm that directly tackles general [MATH]-player games and achieves a [MATH]-approximation for fixed [MATH] and sufficiently large [MATH], where [MATH] is the unique root in [MATH] of [MATH]. Our approach rests on a novel iterative descent-and-repair framework that allows multiple rounds of repair. At the heart of our analysis is a new potential function inspired by continuous-time dynamics, which certifies progress across iterations and ensures polynomial-time termination. Our results highlight the power of history-aware, iterative repair in breaking approximation barriers for multiplayer games.
tldr: The paper introduces a history-aware iterative descent-and-repair algorithm that breaks the one-player-extension barrier for computing approximate Nash equilibria in general multiplayer games.
motivation: Exact Nash equilibrium computation is PPAD-complete, and prior polynomial-time approximation algorithms for general multiplayer games relied on repeated one-player extension, which caps the achievable guarantee at a constant improvement over the classical bound.
method: The authors develop an iterative descent-and-repair framework permitting multiple rounds of repair, analyzed via a new potential function inspired by continuous-time dynamics that certifies progress and guarantees polynomial-time termination.
result: The algorithm achieves a c-approximation for a fixed constant c and sufficiently large number of players, where c is characterized as the unique root of an explicit equation, surpassing the previous barrier.
conclusion: History-aware, iterative repair provides a powerful route to improving approximation guarantees for multiplayer equilibrium computation, beyond what single-shot one-player extensions can deliver.

title: Beyond Identity Creation: Bilinear Sybil Cost In Identities And Time
authors: Homayoun Maleki, Nekane Sainz, Jon Legarda, Igor Santos-Grueiro
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sybil defenses price the creation of an identity, yet influence goes, again and again, to active identities. We study the cost of maintaining influence. A defense has a bilinear Sybil cost with ratio [MATH] if keeping [MATH] identities active for [MATH] periods costs at least [MATH] honest units: the average cost per identity-window is at least [MATH] times an honest participant's cost. Recurrence alone does not guarantee this cost. The cost can be carried over from earlier periods, shared among many identities, or be negligible when fast hardware does the work of thousands of honest devices. We give four sufficient conditions for a defense that checks every identity each period to achieve bilinear Sybil cost: identity binding, freshness, a shared deadline, and sequential, non-batchable work. They yield two guarantees: a bilinear total cost, with [MATH] the speed advantage of the adversary's fastest hardware, and, because the work must be fresh and finished by a common deadline, a bound on the identities active in a period by the processors running at that time. We prove that none of the four follows from the other three. A verifiable delay function on an identity-bound input meets all four without payments, with [MATH] of 2 to 8 for CPUs and about 28 for a hypothetical ASIC, against [MATH] to [MATH] for hash puzzles. We measure one active identity per core per period against about 80,000 under a signed heartbeat, no gain from batching up to 1,000 identities, and rejection of all tested attacks.
tldr: The paper proposes a bilinear Sybil-cost framework for maintaining active identities over time and shows that verifiable delay functions can satisfy four sufficient conditions more efficiently than hash puzzles.
motivation: Existing Sybil defenses focus on the cost of creating identities, but adversaries gain influence by keeping many identities active over time, so the cost of sustained participation needs to be analyzed.
method: The authors formalize bilinear Sybil cost, identify four sufficient conditions (identity binding, freshness, shared deadline, and sequential non-batchable work), prove their independence, and evaluate VDF-based and hash-puzzle-based defenses experimentally.
result: A VDF on identity-bound inputs achieves bilinear cost with ratios of 2–8 for CPUs and about 28 for a hypothetical ASIC, versus lower ratios for hash puzzles; experiments show one active identity per core per period and no batching gain up to 1,000 identities.
conclusion: Maintaining Sybil influence can be made costly through fresh, deadline-bound, sequential work, and VDFs provide a practical construction with strong resistance to batching and hardware advantages.

title: Discovering Like A Scientist: Literature-informed Dimensionless Learning For Physical Closure Of Data-driven Equations
authors: Hao Xu, Tianhao Wu, Dongxiao Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data-driven methods can recover compact equations, yet the physical dependence of their coefficients across operating conditions often remains unresolved. Dimensionless groups can explain this variation, but selecting relevant groups from the many dimensionally admissible combinations remains challenging. Here, we introduce a knowledge-guided framework for dimensionless learning, called {\pi}-former. It learns patterns of variable association and exponent assignment from a corpus of 1,288 established dimensionless groups. Under exact dimensional constraints, the model proposes interpretable basic groups whose combinations are optimized against observations. Across seven physical problems, the framework identifies predictive dimensionless coordinates within seconds. Integration with equation discovery further expresses condition-dependent coefficients through these coordinates, recovering established physical scalings in multi-condition simulations. Applied to experimental measurements of evaporation-driven wetting, the framework discovers dimensionless coordinates and uses them to construct a unified trajectory equation. The resulting model generalizes to held-out conditions across liquids and initial volumes, outperforming existing empirical models. These results establish dimensionless learning as a transferable bridge between accumulated scientific knowledge and data-driven equation discovery, enabling artificial intelligence to uncover physically meaningful laws from observations.
tldr: The paper introduces π-former, a knowledge-guided framework that learns dimensionless groups from a corpus of established physics relations to improve data-driven equation discovery and physical closure.
motivation: Data-driven equation discovery often produces compact equations whose coefficients lack physical interpretation across varying operating conditions, and selecting relevant dimensionless groups from many admissible combinations is difficult.
method: The authors train a model on 1,288 established dimensionless groups to propose interpretable basic groups under exact dimensional constraints, then optimize their combinations against observations and integrate them with equation discovery.
result: Across seven physical problems, the framework identifies predictive dimensionless coordinates within seconds, recovers known physical scalings in multi-condition simulations, and produces a unified trajectory equation for evaporation-driven wetting that generalizes better than empirical models.
conclusion: Dimensionless learning can serve as a transferable bridge between accumulated scientific knowledge and data-driven equation discovery, helping AI uncover physically meaningful laws from observations.

title: Linear Adaptive Variable Time Step Schemes For The Anisotropic Phase Field Dendritic Crystal Growth Model
authors: Ziqi Ma Yayu Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a class of efficient, linear and decoupled adaptive variable time step schemes for the anisotropic phase field dendritic crystal growth model. The main difficulty is twofold: the gradient dependent anisotropic coefficient and the strongly nonlinear terms make unconditional energy stability difficult to achieve, and on nonuniform meshes the discrete energy dissipation law, which is straightforward to establish on uniform meshes, has to be reestablished under varying step sizes. To overcome these difficulties, two linear stabilizers and a time dependent auxiliary variable with relaxation are introduced and incorporated into a second-order generalized BDF-type operator, with the spatial derivatives discretized by the Fourier spectral method. The proposed schemes are energy stable for arbitrary positive adjacent step ratios, so that no restriction on the step ratio is imposed, and only two linear equations together with a few algebraic equations, which are solved independently in Fourier space, need to be solved at each time step. Moreover, the schemes are naturally compatible with energy based time adaptive strategies. The associated adaptive strategy reduces the number of time steps by [MATH]--[MATH] in comparison with uniform time stepping, and numerical experiments on fourfold and sixfold dendritic growth in two dimensions and on three-dimensional growth confirm the accuracy, efficiency and stability of the proposed schemes.
tldr: The paper proposes linear, decoupled adaptive variable time-step schemes for the anisotropic phase field dendritic crystal growth model.
motivation: The anisotropic coefficient and strong nonlinearities make unconditional energy stability difficult, especially on nonuniform meshes where discrete energy dissipation must be reestablished.
method: Two linear stabilizers and a time-dependent relaxed auxiliary variable are combined with a second-order generalized BDF-type operator and Fourier spectral spatial discretization.
result: The schemes are energy stable for arbitrary positive adjacent step ratios, require only linear solves in Fourier space, and reduce time steps by a reported factor compared with uniform stepping in 2D and 3D dendritic growth experiments.
conclusion: The proposed adaptive schemes provide accurate, efficient, and stable numerical simulation of anisotropic dendritic crystal growth.

title: Executable Specifications In Transition Algebra
authors: Daniel G\u{a}in\u{a}, Adri\'{a}n Riesco, Ionu\c{t} \c{t}u\c{t}u
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transition Algebra can be viewed as an extension of many-sorted first-order logic by borrowing essential features from dynamic logic. This leads us to new, more expressive sentences that include transitions labelled with actions, which are built from terms using union, composition, and iteration operators. We define a suitable notion of Horn clause, develop a system of proof rules for reasoning about clauses, and subsequently show that the proof system is sound and complete. We then introduce a rewriting relation based on Horn clauses, capturing transitions along established paths expressed as actions. This rewriting relation is naturally extended to a narrowing procedure for solving queries, thereby laying foundation for logic programming in Transition Algebra. As usual, soundness for both rewriting and narrowing is straightforward, whereas completeness requires additional conditions. Finally, we provide a prototype tool that demonstrates the practical aspects and shows the effectiveness of the proposed method.
tldr: The paper develops executable specifications in Transition Algebra, extending many-sorted first-order logic with dynamic-logic-style actions, Horn clauses, sound and complete proof rules, and a rewriting/narrowing foundation for logic programming.
motivation: The authors aim to make Transition Algebra expressive enough for executable specifications and logic programming by incorporating transitions labelled with structured actions.
method: They define Horn clauses and a proof system for Transition Algebra, establish soundness and completeness, introduce a Horn-clause-based rewriting relation, and extend it to narrowing for query solving.
result: The proof system is shown sound and complete, rewriting and narrowing are sound, and completeness of narrowing requires additional conditions; a prototype tool demonstrates practical effectiveness.
conclusion: Transition Algebra provides a formal foundation for executable specifications and logic programming, but the work is in formal logic and rewriting rather than quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A First Closed-Form Robin Parameter For Optimized Schwarz Waveform Relaxation As A Function Of Iteration Count, Overlap, And Time Window Length
authors: Alejandro Alfonso Rodriguez, Martin J. Gander, Felix Kwok
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Schwarz waveform relaxation (SWR) is a parallel-in-time iterative method for the solution of evolution problems and belongs to the class of Parallel-in-Time algorithms that have received increasing attention over the past three decades. For parabolic problems, SWR converges linearly over long time intervals and exhibits superlinear convergence on short time intervals. Since the introduction of optimized variants (OSWR) nearly three decades ago, determining the optimized Robin parameter when OSWR is applied on bounded time windows has remained an open problem. We introduce here a new analytical approach that, for the first time, yields a closed-form expression for the optimal Robin parameter in the transmission conditions for the one-dimensional heat equation with two overlapping subdomains. The resulting formula explicitly characterizes the dependence of the optimal parameter on the iteration number, the overlap size, and the length of the time window. Beyond resolving this long-standing optimization problem, our analysis provides a framework that can be extended to more general settings, including higher-dimensional problems, multiple subdomains, and higher-order transmission conditions.
tldr: The paper derives a closed-form optimal Robin transmission parameter for optimized Schwarz waveform relaxation applied to the one-dimensional heat equation with two overlapping subdomains.
motivation: Optimized Schwarz waveform relaxation has lacked an analytical expression for the optimal Robin parameter on bounded time windows since its introduction nearly three decades ago.
method: The authors develop a new analytical approach for the one-dimensional heat equation, yielding a closed-form expression for the optimal Robin parameter in terms of iteration count, overlap size, and time-window length.
result: The derived formula explicitly characterizes how the optimal Robin parameter depends on iteration number, overlap, and time-window length, resolving a long-standing open optimization problem.
conclusion: The framework is presented as extendable to higher-dimensional problems, multiple subdomains, and higher-order transmission conditions, though it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Calder\'{o}n's Complex Interpolations Of Variable-exponent Fofana Spaces
authors: Nouffou Diarra, Pokou Nagacy, Sekou Coulibaly
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fofana spaces, introduced in the framework of Wiener amalgam spaces, can be viewed as generalizations of Morrey spaces. These spaces have attracted considerable attention in recent years and have found applications in the study of partial differential equations. In this paper, we investigate their variable-exponent counterparts. More specifically, we describe Calder\'{o}n's, first and second, complex interpolations of Fofana spaces with variable exponent, as well as the corresponding interpolation spaces of their preduals. Our results recover, as special cases, those already known for (classical) Fofana and Morrey spaces.
tldr: The paper characterizes Calderón's first and second complex interpolation methods for Fofana spaces with variable exponent, together with the corresponding interpolation spaces of their preduals.
motivation: Fofana spaces generalize Morrey spaces and have applications in PDE theory, but their variable-exponent variants and interpolation theory remain underdeveloped compared to the classical case.
method: Pure functional-analytic techniques: complex interpolation functors (Calderón's first and second methods) applied to variable-exponent Fofana spaces and duality arguments for their preduals.
result: Explicit descriptions of the interpolation spaces are obtained, recovering known results for classical Fofana and Morrey spaces as special cases.
conclusion: The work extends interpolation theory of Morrey-type spaces to the variable-exponent setting, providing a unified framework with classical results as limits.

title: Discrete Poincar\'e And Bogovskii Operators For Higher Order Finite Element De Rham Complexes
authors: Johnny Guzm\'an, Pratyush Potu, K. Olav Tyssvang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present discrete Poincar\'e and Bogovskii operators for the common finite element discretizations of the de Rham complex of arbitrary polynomial order. We first discuss how such operators arise from a decomposition of the finite element spaces into a lowest order component and a remainder. This results in a fast algorithm for computing grad, curl, and div potentials. We then introduce a nonlocal Poincar\'e operator on contractible domains, which generalizes existing constructions based on cone operators to arbitrary order by integrating over cones against extended test forms. This requires developing commuting extension operators, which turn out to be related to rational forms. We also show how the nonlocal construction is modified to obtain a discrete Bogovskii operator preserving homogeneous boundary conditions. We further discuss how the ideas of the construction fit into the theory of finite element systems.
tldr: The paper constructs discrete Poincaré and Bogovskii operators for higher-order finite element discretizations of the de Rham complex, including a fast potential-computation algorithm.
motivation: Finite element discretizations of the de Rham complex require stable, commuting potential operators (Poincaré, Bogovskii) to control kernels of grad, curl, and div, but existing cone-operator constructions are limited in order and boundary handling.
method: The authors decompose finite element spaces into a lowest-order component plus a remainder to derive fast algorithms for grad/curl/div potentials, then build nonlocal Poincaré operators by integrating over cones against extended test forms, developing commuting extension operators tied to rational forms and adapting the construction to a boundary-preserving discrete Bogovskii operator.
result: The construction yields discrete Poincaré and Bogovskii operators of arbitrary polynomial order on contractible domains, with commuting extension operators and a version that preserves homogeneous boundary conditions, framed within finite element system theory.
conclusion: The framework generalizes cone-operator approaches to arbitrary order and provides practical algorithms for computing potentials, with the machinery fitting naturally into the abstract theory of finite element systems.

title: Learning Coarse Spaces For Two-Grid Methods From Smoothed Errors With Applications To High-Contrast Porous Media Flow
authors: Chenglong Bao, Chen Cui, Ruohua Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient two-grid solvers for high-contrast parametric elliptic problems require coarse spaces that capture error components poorly reduced by local smoothing. As these components vary with the problem parameters, repeatedly constructing parameter-adaptive coarse spaces can be computationally expensive. We propose a coarse-space learning method based on finite-step errors generated by additive Schwarz smoothing. For each training parameter, proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) of smoothed-error snapshots in the discrete energy inner product defines a reference coarse space. A continuous-coordinate neural generator is then trained using a basis-invariant, whitened subspace loss, enabling the prediction of parameter-adaptive coarse spaces on unseen grids. We establish discrete perturbation estimates relating coarse-space discrepancies to the associated nonsymmetric two-grid operators and derive conditional finite-step Krylov residual-polynomial bounds without assuming stationary energy contraction.
