Numerical experiments on high-contrast interface problems, moving-interface Darcy flow, and nonlinear Forchheimer flow demonstrate effective solver performance across varying parameters and grid resolutions. On the finest static test grid, with approximately 264 times as many degrees of freedom as the training grid, the learned spaces achieve FGMRES iteration counts close to those of parameter-specific POD references and comparable to GenEO spaces, while substantially reducing repeated coarse-space construction costs.
tldr: A machine-learning approach that learns parameter-adaptive coarse spaces from smoothed-error snapshots to accelerate two-grid solvers for high-contrast parametric elliptic problems.
motivation: High-contrast parametric elliptic problems need coarse spaces that capture error components poorly reduced by local smoothing, but rebuilding such spaces for every parameter is computationally expensive.
method: POD of smoothed-error snapshots in a discrete energy inner product defines reference coarse spaces, and a continuous-coordinate neural generator is trained with a basis-invariant whitened subspace loss to predict coarse spaces on unseen grids, supported by discrete perturbation and Krylov residual-polynomial bounds.
result: On high-contrast interface problems, moving-interface Darcy flow, and nonlinear Forchheimer flow, learned spaces achieve FGMRES iteration counts close to parameter-specific POD references and comparable to GenEO, even on grids with ~264x more degrees of freedom, while cutting coarse-space construction costs.
conclusion: Learned coarse spaces offer an efficient, generalizable alternative to repeated parameter-specific coarse-space construction for high-contrast multiphysics solvers.

title: Empirical Approximation Of $L^p$ Norms For $p\in (1, 2)$
authors: Egor Kosov Feng Dai
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For [MATH], we prove uniform moment estimates for weighted sums \[ \sum_{j=1}^m\zeta_jw_j|_j,y\rangle|^p \] of independent subgaussian random variables [MATH], where the unit vectors [MATH] and nonnegative weights [MATH] form an isotropic frame. This allows us to obtain optimal sampling discretization of [MATH] norms for each fixed [MATH]. Namely, for an [MATH]-dimensional space [MATH] of bounded functions satisfying [MATH] for every [MATH], we show that [MATH] independent samples [MATH] provide the discretization \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(\xi^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \quad\forall f\in X_N \] with probability at least [MATH]. This implies a corresponding weighted discretization result that, for [MATH], improves Talagrand's bound on the dimension [MATH] needed to embed [MATH]-dimensional subspaces of [MATH] into [MATH] with distortion at most [MATH], giving [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves uniform moment estimates for weighted sums of independent subgaussian random variables over isotropic frames, yielding optimal sampling discretization of L^p norms for 1<p<2 and improved embedding bounds.
motivation: Sampling discretization of L^p norms is a central problem in high-dimensional probability and approximation theory, with applications to embedding finite-dimensional function spaces into discrete L_p^m spaces.
method: The authors establish uniform moment estimates for sums of independent subgaussian random variables weighted by an isotropic frame, then use these estimates to derive a sampling discretization inequality for N-dimensional spaces of bounded functions.
result: They show that m independent samples suffice to discretize the L^p norm within relative error epsilon with high probability, and this yields an improved Talagrand-type bound on the dimension needed to embed N-dimensional subspaces of L^inf into L_1 (or related L_p) with bounded distortion.
conclusion: The work provides optimal-order sampling discretization results for L^p norms in the regime 1<p<2, refining classical embedding estimates; it is a pure mathematics contribution with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Reconstruction And Well-posedness Of An Inverse Coefficient Problem For A Diffusion Equation
authors: Siyu Cen, Bangti Jin, Yavar Kian, Zhi Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the inverse coefficient problem of determining an unknown coefficient in a diffusion equation from a single boundary flux measurement. More precisely, assuming that the domain is cylindrical, we develop a unified theoretical and numerical framework for the stable reconstruction of a space-time-dependent coefficient, by reformulating the inverse problem as a nonlinear equation. The inherent nonlinearity of the problem is transferred to an auxiliary nonlinear equation, enabling the application of techniques and concepts from nonlinear analysis. By combining representation formulas with regularity properties of solutions to diffusion equations, we extend to nonlinear inverse problems an approach that has so far been restricted to linear ones. The theoretical reconstruction procedure is complemented by a numerical analysis of the proposed method, including convergence and error estimates, as well as numerical experiments. The proposed reconstruction algorithm is directly inspired by the theoretical framework.
tldr: The paper develops a unified theoretical and numerical framework for stably reconstructing a space-time-dependent coefficient in a cylindrical-domain diffusion equation from a single boundary flux measurement.
motivation: Inverse coefficient problems for diffusion equations are severely ill-posed and typically treated with linearized or heavily regularized approaches; the authors seek a stable, provably convergent reconstruction scheme for the genuinely nonlinear version.
method: The inverse problem is reformulated as a nonlinear operator equation, transferring the nonlinearity into an auxiliary equation so that nonlinear-analysis tools (representation formulas plus solution regularity for diffusion equations) can be applied; convergence and error estimates are derived and matched to a numerical algorithm.
result: The approach extends a technique previously limited to linear inverse problems to the nonlinear setting, yielding stable reconstruction with convergence guarantees and supporting numerical experiments.
conclusion: The framework provides a principled theoretical and computational basis for nonlinear inverse coefficient identification in diffusion, with the algorithm directly inspired by the analysis.

title: The Convergence Rate Of Accelerated Proximal Gradient Methods With General Inertia Term For Convex Composite Multiobjective Optimization
authors: Chengzhi Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study accelerated proximal gradient methods with general stepsizes for convex composite multiobjective optimization, in which every objective is the sum of a smooth convex term and a proper closed convex extended-valued term, and the proximal subproblem retains a separate offset for each objective. The momentum coefficient may depend on the computed trajectory. For a two-parameter root momentum rule we prove boundedness, weighted square summability of the displacements, a merit-function rate of [MATH], and displacement decay of [MATH] whenever the first parameter converges to a value in [MATH]; the second parameter need not converge or have bounded total variation. The analysis is organized as a chain of basic estimates, an energy identity, coefficient asymptotics, and auxiliary lemmas that are reused in every regime. For the critical parameter [MATH] we establish the finite bound [MATH], square summability of the displacements, displacement decay [MATH], and convergence of the full sequence to a weak Pareto point. The remaining little-o question at [MATH] is shown to be exactly the vanishing of a nonnegative critical energy, so it is separated from the large-[MATH] estimate rather than left as a missing step. For [MATH] we give the rate [MATH] and for every [MATH] the qualitative conclusion [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH]. A table summarizes the rate picture over the whole positive range of [MATH], and a JOS1 experiment illustrates the predicted little-[MATH] separation.
tldr: A purely classical optimization paper establishing convergence rates for accelerated proximal gradient methods with general inertia/momentum rules applied to convex composite multiobjective problems.
motivation: Accelerated proximal gradient schemes with trajectory-dependent momentum coefficients lack a unified convergence analysis for multiobjective composite settings, motivating a systematic rate theory across parameter regimes.
method: The authors analyze a two-parameter root momentum rule via a chain of basic estimates, an energy identity, coefficient asymptotics, and reusable auxiliary lemmas, covering subcritical, critical, and supercritical parameter ranges.
result: They prove boundedness, weighted square summability of displacements, merit-function rates, displacement decay, and — at the critical parameter — convergence of the full sequence to a weak Pareto point, with a JOS1 experiment illustrating the predicted little-o separation.
conclusion: The work delivers a complete rate picture over the positive parameter range and reduces the remaining little-o question to the vanishing of a nonnegative critical energy.

title: Optimal Error Estimates With Polynomial Dependence On $\epsilon^{-1}$ For Mixed Finite Element Methods Of The Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes System
authors: Haijun Gao, Xi Li, Xiaoli Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we analyze a first-order convex-splitting mixed finite element scheme for the Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes system, tracking explicitly how the error constants depend on the interface width [MATH]. Due to the strong nonlinear coupling inherent in the CHNS system and the singular dependence of the Cahn--Hilliard equation on [MATH], conventional energy-based analyzes often lead to severe dependence of the error constants on [MATH], and may even result in exponential growth. Such dependence significantly limits the applicability of the resulting error estimates in the small-interfacial-thickness regime. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a robust parameter error analysis framework with respect to interfacial thickness [MATH]. In particular, by introducing [MATH] approximation properties for the Ritz projection and the Ritz and Stokes quasi-projection operators, together with spectral-type estimates for the discrete perturbed Cahn--Hilliard operator, we effectively control the singular terms arising from the interfacial thickness parameter in the error analysis. Compared with the classical results, which address only the Allen-Cahn or Cahn-Hilliard equation, we adopt a three-term discrete Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality analysis technique and achieve a substantial reduction in the degree of polynomial dependence for the coupled system. Numerical experiments are presented to verify the effectiveness of the theoretical results and to demonstrate the robustness of the method for different parameters of interfacial thickness.
tldr: This paper develops a mixed finite element error analysis for the Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes system with error constants that depend polynomially on the inverse interface width.
motivation: Conventional energy-based error analyses for the strongly coupled Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes system can yield severe or exponential dependence on the small interface-width parameter, limiting applicability in the sharp-interface regime.
method: The authors analyze a first-order convex-splitting mixed finite element scheme and introduce approximation properties for Ritz and Stokes quasi-projection operators plus spectral-type estimates for the discrete perturbed Cahn-Hilliard operator, using a three-term discrete Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality.
result: The analysis yields optimal error estimates with substantially reduced polynomial dependence on the inverse interface width compared with classical results, and numerical experiments verify the theory and robustness across interface-width parameters.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides robust parameter-dependent error control for the coupled CHNS system in the small-interface-thickness regime.

title: Quasi-norms On $\mathbb{R}^d$: Characterization And Approximation By Conic Splines
authors: Michael Unser
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We first show that a regularizer on [MATH] that is continuous, symmetric, and amplitude-equivariant is of the form [MATH] with [MATH], where [MATH] is continuous and absolutely homogeneous; we call the set of such [MATH] the CH class, whose convex members are the seminorms. Within the CH class, we single out two configurations of interest for regularization: the quasi-norms, which are exactly the positive-definite members of the family, and the quasi-seminorms with null space control, which are the composition of a quasi-norm with a linear map that sets the null space. We then propose a universal parametrization of the class by conic splines, the continuous functions that are linear on each cone of a polyhedral fan. Specifically, we show that the polyhedral CH functionals are exactly the symmetric non-negative conic splines, and that these admit a stable nodal representation in a basis of conic B-splines. Finally, we determine the rates of approximation: the conic spline interpolant converges at the second-order rate [MATH], in the [MATH]-norm on the hyper-sphere when the angular profile is twice differentiable, and in the [MATH]-norm when its spherical Hessian variation is bounded, which covers the polyhedral members of the class. The rate is sharp, already for the Euclidean norm. The planar case is worked out in full, with the trigonometric hat functions as basis and an [MATH]-norm of second differences as regularity index.
tldr: The paper characterizes symmetric amplitude-equivariant regularizers on R^d as quasi-norms or quasi-seminorms and approximates them using conic splines.
motivation: The work aims to provide a systematic mathematical framework for regularizers used in regularization theory, particularly quasi-norms and their parametrization.
method: It introduces the CH class of continuous, symmetric, amplitude-equivariant functionals, identifies positive-definite members as quasi-norms, and represents polyhedral CH functionals via symmetric non-negative conic splines with a stable B-spline basis.
result: Conic spline interpolation achieves second-order approximation rates in the L^2 norm on the hypersphere under differentiability conditions and in the L^∞ norm for bounded spherical Hessian variation, with sharp rates even for the Euclidean norm.
conclusion: The proposed conic spline framework offers a universal and stable parametrization of quasi-norms and quasi-seminorms, with sharp approximation guarantees and a complete planar case.

title: Calmness Modulus Of Parameterized Convex Constraint Systems: Exact Closed-Form Formulas Via Second-Order Admissibility
authors: Jes\'us Camacho
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We resolve the open problem of deriving an exact, closed-form algebraic formula for the calmness modulus of [MATH] convex constrained feasible set mappings [MATH] under right-hand side perturbations at a given pair of the graph [MATH]. First, under the condition [MATH], we prove that the calmness modulus coincides with the inverse distance from the origin to the boundary of the nominal subdifferential. Second, for general [MATH] convex systems where the previously mentioned interior condition does not hold, we introduce a second-order admissibility filtering over the active indexes. We show that this filtered family, [MATH], yields an exact characterization of the calmness modulus relying solely on nominal data.
tldr: The paper derives exact closed-form formulas for the calmness modulus of parameterized convex constrained feasible-set mappings under right-hand-side perturbations.
motivation: The calmness modulus is a key quantitative stability measure in variational analysis and optimization, but an exact algebraic formula based solely on nominal data was previously an open problem.
method: The authors first show that under an interior-type condition the calmness modulus equals the inverse distance from the origin to the boundary of the nominal subdifferential, then introduce a second-order admissibility filtering over active indices for the general convex case.
result: The filtered active-index family yields an exact characterization of the calmness modulus relying only on nominal problem data, matching the interior-case formula when the condition holds.
conclusion: The work settles a long-standing open question in stability theory of convex constraint systems and provides computable closed-form expressions for calmness moduli.

title: Aqua - A Modular Authentication Quality Modeling Framework
authors: Alex R. Mattukat, Michael Zerbe, Krisa Carka
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Authentication solutions are the key design, architectural, and implementation decisions that implement authentication security controls. An example is a password-based authentication solution. While researchers often examine authentication quality, existing approaches do not distinguish which effects on quality stem from which aspect of authentication. For example, multi-factor authentication solutions tend to be less usable because they combine multiple authenticators, whereas passkeys are more secure than passwords because of properties inherent to the authenticator itself. This paper presents AQUA, a modular quality modeling framework for authentication solutions. AQUA's core idea is to decompose authentication into four interrelated concepts, enabling modular specification of authentication quality and tracing quality effects back to their source. We demonstrate AQUA with initial definitional quality models that address the levels of authenticators, authentication techniques, and authentication solutions. We further illustrate the interrelations between these concepts through concrete examples and a usability metric, showing how quality propagates across the concepts and ultimately affects the overall quality of an authentication solution. Our results provide a foundation for future work, including designing assessment and prediction models for authentication solutions and automated quality assessments.
tldr: AQUA is a modular framework that decomposes authentication solutions into four interrelated concepts so that quality attributes (security, usability) can be specified and traced back to their source components.
motivation: Existing authentication-quality research treats solutions monolithically, making it impossible to attribute observed quality effects to specific aspects such as the authenticator type or the combination of factors.
method: The authors define a layered decomposition of authentication (authenticators, authentication techniques, authentication solutions) and provide initial definitional quality models plus a usability metric illustrating how quality propagates across levels.
result: Concrete examples show how quality attributes propagate from the authenticator level up to overall solution quality, yielding a modular specification that separates inherent authenticator properties from composition effects.
conclusion: The framework establishes a foundation for future assessment and prediction models and automated quality evaluation of authentication solutions.

title: Sundance: A Simple Smt Solver For Program Verification
authors: Amar Shah, Benjamin F. Jones, Can Cebeci, Jason Z. S. Hu, Lee A. Barnett, R\'emi Delmas, Marijn Heule, Bryan Parno, Bruno Dutertre
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Sundance, an SMT solver for program verification written in about 13,600 lines of Rust. Sundance combines the Cadical SAT solver with congruence closure, linear arithmetic, algebraic datatypes, and pattern-based quantifier instantiation. Sundance produces eDRAT proofs for every unsat answer. On 21,531 queries from Verus, Dafny, and F*, Sundance is comparable to existing solvers, with 26--38 times fewer lines of code than Z3 and cvc5. We further show that its components can be swapped for Z3's arithmetic solver, MiniSat, and the Semper e-graph. We have open sourced Sundance.
tldr: Sundance is a compact Rust-based SMT solver for program verification that combines CaDiCaL with congruence closure, linear arithmetic, algebraic datatypes, quantifier instantiation, and eDRAT proof production.
motivation: Program verification relies on SMT solvers, but existing tools like Z3 and cvc5 are large and complex. The authors aim to build a simpler, verifiable, and extensible solver without sacrificing practical performance.
method: Sundance integrates a SAT solver with theory solvers for congruence closure, linear arithmetic, algebraic datatypes, and pattern-based quantifier instantiation, and emits eDRAT proofs for unsatisfiable answers.
result: On 21,531 verification queries from Verus, Dafny, and F*, Sundance performs comparably to established solvers while using 26–38 times fewer lines of code, and its components can be swapped with Z3 arithmetic, MiniSat, and the Semper e-graph.
conclusion: Sundance demonstrates that a simple, open-source SMT solver can be competitive for program verification while remaining modular and proof-producing.

title: Timing Is Everything: Inferring Temporal Membership In Continually Updated Models
authors: Jie Fu, Xiangpeng Deng, Yuan Hong, Wendy Hui Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continual model updating has become a common practice in the deployment of machine learning systems. However, the dynamic training behaviors give rise to new risks not sufficiently addressed by existing studies. In this paper, we present the first systematic study of temporal privacy risk in continually updated deep learning models. We formalize the notion of temporal membership in continually updated models. We then define the temporal membership inference attack, which seeks to infer whether and when individual samples were involved in model training, at both timestamp-level and interval-level granularities. To this end, we propose TMIA, a novel black-box attack that leverages bidirectional LSTMs to infer temporal membership from model outputs observed across successive updates. Through extensive experiments on three language models and three image classification models, we show that TMIA is highly effective and significantly outperforms existing baselines. Finally, we evaluate three potential defenses, revealing the trade-off between privacy protection and model utility.
tldr: This paper introduces temporal membership inference attacks (TMIA) that determine whether and when individual data samples were used to train continually updated deep learning models.
motivation: Continual model updating is now routine in deployed ML systems, but the dynamic retraining behaviour creates privacy risks—such as inferring the timing of data inclusion—that existing membership inference studies do not address.
method: The authors formalize temporal membership at timestamp and interval granularity and propose TMIA, a black-box attack using bidirectional LSTMs over model outputs observed across successive model updates.
result: Experiments on three language models and three image classifiers show TMIA substantially outperforms existing baselines, and an evaluation of three defenses exposes a privacy–utility trade-off.
conclusion: Temporal membership is a genuine and previously unstudied privacy leakage channel in continually updated models, requiring dedicated defenses.

title: A Hybrid Approach For Automated Security Pattern Recovery
authors: Anh Minh Nguyen, Tuan Dat Tran, Alzubair Hassan, Liliana Pasquale
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Security-by-design emphasises integrating security into software design and development. Security pattern catalogues operationalise this principle by prescribing reusable architectural solutions to recurring security problems. However, recovering their implementations from source code remains challenging because security patterns are abstract, span multiple components, and admit many valid implementations. We present SecPatRec, a hybrid approach for automated security pattern recovery from source code repositories. We treat a security pattern as a reference architecture and frame its recovery as a deductive task: determining which prescribed roles are present, grounding them in code entities, and recovering their interaction sequences. SecPatRec pairs a ReAct-style LLM agent equipped with semantic and lexical code search for role detection and grounding with static code property graph analysis for interaction recovery. We curate a human-validated ground-truth dataset of 100 pattern instances covering five security patterns across 93 open-source Java and Python repositories, and introduce a three-level evaluation framework measuring recovery correctness against this ground truth. We evaluate SecPatRec using four LLMs, including proprietary and open-source models. Averaged over all models and pattern instances, SecPatRec achieves role-detection accuracy of 0.84, role-grounding similarity of 0.84, and an interaction-recovery score of 0.66. Compared to a one-shot end-to-end LLM baseline, SecPatRec achieves higher aggregate recovery scores and lower estimated LLM API costs per run, while processing repositories that exceed the baseline's configured input limit. The recovered role mappings and statically derived interaction sequences provide structural and behavioural evidence that can support inspection of security-pattern implementations.
tldr: SecPatRec is a hybrid LLM-agent plus static-analysis tool that recovers security pattern implementations (roles, groundings, interaction sequences) from Java and Python source code repositories.
motivation: Security-by-design relies on reusable security pattern catalogues, but detecting where such abstract, multi-component patterns are actually implemented in real code is difficult because many valid implementations exist.
method: The authors treat a security pattern as a reference architecture and cast recovery as a deductive task, pairing a ReAct-style LLM agent with semantic and lexical code search for role detection/grounding and code property graph analysis for interaction recovery; they also build a 100-instance human-validated ground-truth dataset across five patterns and 93 repositories.
result: Across four LLMs, SecPatRec reaches 0.84 role-detection accuracy, 0.84 role-grounding similarity and 0.66 interaction-recovery score, outperforming a one-shot end-to-end LLM baseline at lower estimated API cost and handling repositories beyond the baseline's input limit.
conclusion: The recovered role mappings and static interaction sequences provide structural and behavioural evidence useful for inspecting security-pattern implementations, showing hybrid LLM/static-analysis pipelines are practical for software security auditing.

title: Dimensionally Absolutely Stable But Non-diagonalizable $T$-meshes
authors: Mao Shi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an infinite family of rectangular \(T\)-meshes whose conformality-vector-space dimension is constant over all structurally similar geometric realizations, although the meshes are not diagonalizable. For every integer \(d\ge 2\), the construction has \(2(d+2)\) \(\Tl\)-edges and intersection graph \(K_{d+2,d+2}\). Every \(\Tl\)-edge contains at least \(d+2\) vertices, so no edge is vanishable under the usual vertex-count criterion for bidegree \((d,d)\) and smoothness \((d-1,d-1)\). We prove that the conformality-vector space is one-dimensional throughout the structural similarity class. Its generator is the outer product of two vectors of barycentric interpolation weights, extended by four zero coordinates. Non-diagonalizability follows by examining the last edge in any proposed diagonalizing ordering. Thus, for the geometric structural similarity class specified here, diagonalizability is not a necessary condition for dimensional absolute stability.
tldr: The paper constructs an infinite family of rectangular T-meshes with constant conformality-vector-space dimension despite being non-diagonalizable.
motivation: It investigates whether diagonalizability is a necessary condition for dimensional absolute stability in T-meshes.
method: The authors build T-meshes with 2(d+2) Tl-edges and intersection graph K_{d+2,d+2}, then prove the conformality-vector space is one-dimensional throughout the structural similarity class and analyze non-diagonalizability via edge ordering.
result: For every d ≥ 2, the constructed meshes have a one-dimensional conformality vector space generated by an outer product of barycentric interpolation weights extended by zeros, and are non-diagonalizable.
conclusion: Within the specified geometric structural similarity class, diagonalizability is not necessary for dimensional absolute stability of T-meshes.

title: The Power And Limits Of Money Burning In Bilateral Trade
authors: Moshe Babaioff, Noam Nisan, Ariel Shaulker
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the power of money burning in bilateral trade. In this problem, a seller owns an indivisible item, a buyer would like to acquire it, and each of these two traders has a private value for the item and the values are sampled from independent distributions. We ask whether the traders can benefit from a mechanism that burns money, that is, one that charges the buyer more than it pays the seller, so that neither trader enjoys the difference (money burnt is a loss for the traders). Is it possible that the traders will ever be better off if the trade mechanism can burn money? For Bayesian incentive-compatible mechanisms and for deterministic dominant-strategy incentive-compatible (DSIC) mechanisms, it is known that money burning is always a waste and can only hurt the traders. Maybe surprisingly, we show that once a DSIC mechanism can use randomization, money burning can significantly benefit the traders, and the gain of each of them can be arbitrarily large. In contrast, we show that the power of DSIC randomized mechanisms that burn money is still very limited in the sense that they cannot guarantee any constant fraction of the first-best gains-from-trade.
tldr: The paper studies when money-burning mechanisms can improve outcomes in bilateral trade, showing randomized DSIC mechanisms can benefit traders arbitrarily much but still cannot guarantee a constant fraction of first-best gains-from-trade.
motivation: Prior work shows money burning is wasteful for Bayesian incentive-compatible and deterministic DSIC mechanisms in bilateral trade; the authors ask whether randomization changes this conclusion.
method: The authors analyze mechanism design for bilateral trade with independent private values, comparing Bayesian IC, deterministic DSIC, and randomized DSIC mechanisms that may burn money.
result: Randomized DSIC mechanisms with money burning can make each trader arbitrarily better off, yet they cannot guarantee any constant fraction of the first-best gains-from-trade.
conclusion: Money burning has significant but limited power under randomized DSIC: it can improve trader welfare unboundedly in some cases but cannot provide robust constant-factor approximation to first-best efficiency.

title: Boundary Phenomena For Slow Recurrences:finite And Infinite Critical Sets
authors: Mohsen Aliabadi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a second-order recurrence with positive integral coefficients, the slow length of an integer is the largest index at which it can occur when the initial terms range over positive integers. Spiro conjectured that, among a finite set of relatively prime recurrence pairs, a pair is slowest infinitely often precisely when its growth constant is strictly less than the square of the smallest growth constant. We study the equality case. For [MATH], the larger-growth pair attains the maximal slow length, with ties allowed, on [MATH] integers up to [MATH] whenever [MATH], whereas for [MATH] its complete set of slowest integers is [MATH]. We give certificates for the infinite examples and prove a bounded-seed theorem that limits the possible initial pairs at each critical index.
tldr: The paper studies the equality case in Spiro's conjecture on slow lengths of second-order recurrences with positive integer coefficients, characterizing finite and infinite critical sets.
motivation: Spiro conjectured that among relatively prime recurrence pairs the slowest one is determined by having growth constant strictly below the square of the smallest growth constant; the equality case where this criterion degenerates was left open.
method: The author constructs explicit certificates for infinite families of slowest integers and proves a bounded-seed theorem that restricts the possible initial value pairs at each critical index.
result: For the parameter value M=9 the larger-growth pair attains maximal slow length (with ties) on all integers up to a bound whenever a stated condition holds, while for M=8 the complete set of slowest integers is determined explicitly.
conclusion: The findings extend Spiro's conjecture into the equality regime and provide structural constraints (bounded seeds) governing critical sets of slow recurrences.

title: Generalized Disjunctive Programming With Derivative-Free Configuration Search
authors: Albert Joon Lee, Woosik Kim, David E. Bernal Neira
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generalized disjunctive programming (GDP) describes process design alternatives with Boolean variables, disjunctions, and logical propositions, and fixing one configuration leaves a subproblem in the continuous variables. Conventional GDP methods require explicit equations, which a simulator may not expose, and mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) reformulations can be intractable for nonconvex models. The external-variable reformulation turns configuration choice into an optimization over an integer lattice whose objective is the subproblem value, which derivative-free optimization (DFO) can search while the GDP model continues describing the alternatives. We pair GDP models with surrogate DFO methods and the direct-search method NOMAD and compare them with discrete steepest descent (D-SDA), logic-based and MINLP solvers, and enumeration on nine process models, 21 test functions, a pharmaceutical flowsheet simulated in PharmaPy, and a catalytic distillation column with 100,947 configurations. On the largest reactor network, the surrogate methods MISO and RBFOpt reach the reference in nine or ten of ten runs with about 30 subproblem solves, whereas logic-based methods solve nearly one subproblem for each admissible configuration and most D-SDA descents end at one local minimum. In the flowsheet example, where GDP solvers do not apply, RBFOpt and MISO find the best of 36 simulated configurations in every run with 20 evaluations. For the catalytic column, D-SDA and MISO reach the best known design with 100 evaluations, whereas MINLP solvers find no design within 15% of it and global solvers return contradictory certificates. This search pays off when the configuration space is too large to enumerate, has deceptive local minima, or has MINLP reformulations that fail, and enumeration or a direct reformulation is simpler for small algebraic models.
tldr: This paper couples generalized disjunctive programming (GDP) models with derivative-free/surrogate optimization to search large discrete configuration spaces when algebraic reformulations are unavailable or intractable.
motivation: Conventional GDP methods need explicit equations and MINLP reformulations, which fail when models are simulator-based, nonconvex, or have huge configuration lattices.
method: The external-variable reformulation turns configuration choice into optimization over an integer lattice evaluated by subproblem solves; the authors pair GDP models with surrogate DFO (MISO, RBFOpt) and direct search (NOMAD), benchmarking against D-SDA, logic-based/MINLP solvers, and enumeration.
result: On nine process models, 21 test functions, a PharmaPy flowsheet, and a catalytic distillation column with 100,947 configurations, surrogate DFO reaches reference optima in far fewer subproblem solves than logic-based or MINLP approaches, which often fail or return contradictory certificates.
conclusion: Derivative-free configuration search is advantageous for large, deceptive, or reformulation-resistant configuration spaces, while enumeration or direct reformulation remains simpler for small algebraic models.

title: Mixed-Integer Second-Order Cone Formulations For The Euclidean Bottleneck Steiner Tree Problem In $\mathbb{R}^d$
authors: Gabriel P. Braun, Marcia Fampa, Nelson Maculan, Renan V. Pinto
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a set of terminals in [MATH] and an integer [MATH], the Euclidean bottleneck Steiner tree problem (EBSTP) asks for a tree spanning the terminals with at most [MATH] Steiner points that minimizes its longest edge. Although the planar case has been widely studied, exact optimization methods for arbitrary dimension remain scarce. We develop two exact mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) formulations for the EBSTP: a single-commodity flow formulation and a formulation with connectivity cuts. Both formulations share a geometric core based on edge-conditional second-order cone constraints and are strengthened by problem-specific preprocessing, edge-dependent big-[MATH] constants, symmetry-breaking constraints, constructive upper bounds, and new global lower bounds on the optimal value. We establish the correctness of the formulations and prove the validity of all strengthening techniques. Computational experiments on 1050 benchmark instances in dimensions [MATH], with up to [MATH] terminals and [MATH] Steiner points, show that the single-commodity flow formulation consistently outperforms the formulation with connectivity cuts, with an advantage { in solved instances} that grows with dimension. The proposed global lower bounds substantially strengthen the root relaxation, while the single-commodity flow formulation provides the most robust exact solution method across all test sets. These results establish the single-commodity flow formulation as an effective exact approach for the EBSTP in arbitrary fixed dimension.
tldr: The paper develops two exact mixed-integer second-order cone programming formulations for the Euclidean bottleneck Steiner tree problem in arbitrary dimension d, with strengthening techniques and benchmark comparisons.
motivation: Exact optimization methods for the Euclidean bottleneck Steiner tree problem remain scarce for dimensions beyond the planar case, so the authors aim to provide general-dimensional exact formulations.
method: Two MISOCP formulations are proposed—a single-commodity flow formulation and a connectivity-cut formulation—both built on edge-conditional second-order cone constraints and enhanced with preprocessing, edge-dependent big-M constants, symmetry breaking, constructive upper bounds, and new global lower bounds.
result: Across 1050 benchmark instances in dimensions d=2-5 with up to dozens of terminals and Steiner points, the single-commodity flow formulation consistently outperforms the connectivity-cut formulation, with an advantage that grows with dimension, and the new global lower bounds substantially tighten the root relaxation.
conclusion: The single-commodity flow MISOCP is established as a robust exact approach for the Euclidean bottleneck Steiner tree problem in arbitrary fixed dimension.

title: Parabolic Extrapolation Of Compactness With Applications To Characterizations Of The Parabolic Cmo Space Via Parabolic Fractional Commutators
authors: Mingming Cao, Weiyi Kong, Dachun Yang, Wen Yuan, Chenfeng Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we prove two compactness parabolic extrapolation theorems for linear operators and their commutators on parabolic weighted Lebesgue spaces. As applications, we show that [MATH] (parabolic CMO space) if and only if [MATH] and the commutator [MATH] is compact from [MATH] to [MATH] for any [MATH], [MATH] with [MATH], and [MATH] (parabolic Muckenhoupt class), where [MATH] is the parabolic fractional integral. Several other equivalent characterizations of the space [MATH] are also given. Our approach combines the unweighted compactness for mixed commutators, a local lower estimate for [MATH], and both a quantitative Uchiyama-type description and the equivalence with [MATH] of [MATH], where the infimum is taken over all compact operators [MATH]. Finally, we establish two parabolic weighted Fr\'echet--Kolmogorov compactness criteria, which further induce a parabolic interpolation theorem of compactness.
tldr: This paper proves parabolic extrapolation theorems for compactness of linear operators and their commutators on parabolic weighted Lebesgue spaces, and uses these to characterize a parabolic CMO space via compactness of parabolic fractional commutators.
motivation: The authors aim to extend extrapolation-of-compactness techniques to the parabolic (time-dependent, non-doubling) setting in order to obtain new compact-commutator characterizations of parabolic BMO/CMO-type spaces.
method: The approach combines unweighted compactness for mixed commutators, a local lower estimate for the parabolic fractional integral, a quantitative Uchiyama-type description, and an infimum-over-compact-operators equivalence, together with two parabolic weighted Frechet-Kolmogorov compactness criteria.
result: They establish two compactness parabolic extrapolation theorems and show that a function lies in the parabolic CMO space if and only if it belongs to the relevant parabolic BMO-type space and its commutator with the parabolic fractional integral is compact on parabolic weighted Lebesgue spaces for all admissible weights in the parabolic Muckenhoupt class.
conclusion: The work provides several equivalent characterizations of the parabolic CMO space and a parabolic interpolation theorem of compactness, advancing the real-variable harmonic analysis toolbox for parabolic geometries.

title: Wandering Continua, Renormalization, And Lebesgue Measure On Julia Sets
authors: Willie Rush Lim
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Lebesgue measure of wandering continua and related invariant sets in Julia sets, using the hyperbolic area method recently developed by Ye. For entire functions of finite type, we show that a wandering continuum of positive area must escape to infinity uniformly. For infinitely renormalizable unicritical polynomials, we show that almost every point in the renormalization core (the intersection of the orbits of little Julia sets) is recurrent and contained in the postcritical set. The main tool is a conservativity theorem: if [MATH] is injective on a forward invariant measurable subset [MATH] of the Julia set, then [MATH] is conservative and almost every point of [MATH] is recurrent and contained in the postsingular set.
tldr: A pure holomorphic dynamics paper proving measure-theoretic and conservativity results for wandering continua and renormalization cores in Julia sets of entire and unicritical polynomial maps.
motivation: Understanding the Lebesgue measure and recurrence properties of wandering continua and invariant sets in Julia sets addresses open questions in transcendental and polynomial complex dynamics.
method: Uses Ye's hyperbolic area method together with a conservativity theorem for injective maps on forward-invariant measurable subsets of the Julia set.
result: Wandering continua of positive area in finite-type entire functions must escape to infinity uniformly, and for infinitely renormalizable unicritical polynomials almost every point of the renormalization core is recurrent and lies in the postcritical set.
conclusion: The work establishes general conservativity and recurrence criteria that unify several measure-theoretic phenomena in complex dynamics, with no connection to quantum information science.

title: Geometric Multigrid Preconditioners For Conforming Finite Element Methods On Arbitrarily Agglomerated Meshes
authors: Jordi Manyer Santiago Badia
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Geometric multigrid methods for conforming finite element discretisations classically require a nested mesh hierarchy, forcing coarse meshes to be conforming, which is unsuitable for general domains. In order to eliminate this geometric constraint, we introduce and analyse a family of multilevel auxiliary space preconditioners. At the first level, a conforming Lagrangian discretisation on a fine simplicial mesh is preconditioned by a non-conforming polytopal discretisation posed on an arbitrarily agglomerated coarse mesh. At the subsequent levels, the coarse problem is solved by a geometric multigrid method for that polytopal discretisation on further agglomerated meshes, so that the whole hierarchy is generated from the fine mesh by agglomeration alone. We consider two polytopal discretisations, a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method and a hybrid high-order method. The prolongation operator at the first level is an element-wise interpolation onto the fine mesh followed by nodal averaging, preceded in the hybrid high-order case by a local potential reconstruction. For point-Jacobi and vertex-star patch additive Schwarz smoothers, we prove that the condition number of the preconditioned system is bounded by [MATH], where [MATH] is the coarsening ratio, and by [MATH] for the DG variant with penalty proportional to [MATH]. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions, on structured and unstructured meshes with agglomerates generated by automatic clustering algorithms, confirm the robustness of the preconditioners.
tldr: The paper introduces and analyzes multilevel auxiliary space preconditioners that replace the nested conforming coarse-mesh requirement of geometric multigrid with arbitrarily agglomerated polytopal discretisations.
motivation: Geometric multigrid for conforming finite element methods classically requires nested, conforming coarse meshes, which is impractical on general domains; the authors aim to remove this geometric constraint.
method: A conforming Lagrangian fine-mesh discretisation is preconditioned at the first level by a non-conforming polytopal discretisation (symmetric interior penalty DG or hybrid high-order) on agglomerated coarse meshes, with further levels solved by geometric multigrid on progressively agglomerated meshes; prolongation uses element-wise interpolation with nodal averaging, and condition-number bounds are proved for point-Jacobi and vertex-star patch additive Schwarz smoothers.
result: The preconditioned system's condition number is proven bounded by a constant depending only on the coarsening ratio (and by an analogous bound for the DG variant with penalty proportional to the inverse of that ratio), and 2D/3D numerical experiments on structured and unstructured agglomerated meshes confirm robustness.
conclusion: Multigrid hierarchies can be built purely by agglomeration from a single fine mesh, yielding robust, provably well-conditioned solvers for conforming finite element discretisations on general domains.

title: Flux-Matched Poisson Iteration For Generated Jacobian Equations: Local Convergence And Spectral Galerkin Approximation
authors: Yixuan Zhang Haoxiang Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a flux-matched Poisson iteration for solving generated Jacobian equations with second boundary conditions. In each step, it solves a fixed shifted Poisson problem with a Neumann-type boundary condition. Near a smooth regular solution with positive [MATH] densities, we prove that the iteration has local geometric convergence in [MATH] on smooth connected Riemannian domains. The iteration is then discretized using a spectral Galerkin method, with local convergence proved for the Fourier-Jacobi scheme on spherical caps. Optical numerical experiments support these estimates and demonstrate useful imaging performance beyond the local convergence theory.
tldr: The paper introduces a flux-matched Poisson iteration with spectral Galerkin discretization for numerically solving generated Jacobian equations under second boundary conditions.
motivation: Generated Jacobian equations generalize optimal transport and require robust numerical solvers; the authors seek a convergent iterative scheme with provable local convergence on smooth Riemannian domains.
method: Each iteration solves a shifted Poisson problem with Neumann-type boundary conditions; the scheme is then discretized via a Fourier-Jacobi spectral Galerkin method on spherical caps, with local geometric convergence proven in Sobolev norms.
result: Local geometric convergence is established near smooth regular solutions with positive densities, and optical numerical experiments confirm the convergence estimates while showing good imaging performance beyond the theoretical regime.
conclusion: The flux-matched Poisson iteration offers a theoretically grounded and practically effective numerical approach to generated Jacobian equations, particularly in optical imaging applications.

title: Equilibrium Webs And Stability For Arbitrary Families Of Endomorphisms Of Projective Spaces
authors: Fabrizio Bianchi, Zhuchao Ji, Junyi Xie
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider arbitrary holomorphic families of endomorphisms of a complex projective space. We prove that the existence of an equilibrium web implies the holomorphic motion of all repelling cycles contained in the Julia set, i.e., the support of the unique measure of maximal entropy. Together with previous results of Berteloot, Bianchi, Br\'evard, Buff, and Dupont, this completes the extension of the stability-bifurcation theory to arbitrary families of holomorphic endomorphisms. The same conclusions also hold for holomorphic families of polynomial-like maps of large topological degree.
tldr: The paper proves that the existence of an equilibrium web for arbitrary holomorphic families of endomorphisms of complex projective space implies holomorphic motion of all repelling cycles in the Julia set, completing the stability-bifurcation theory for such families.
motivation: Stability and bifurcation theory for holomorphic families of endomorphisms was known only in restricted settings; the authors aim to extend it to fully arbitrary families via the notion of equilibrium webs.
method: Purely complex-analytic and dynamical techniques: equilibrium (canonical) webs of currents, the unique measure of maximal entropy and its support Julia set, and holomorphic motion arguments for repelling periodic cycles, plus polynomial-like maps of large topological degree.
result: Existence of an equilibrium web is shown to force holomorphic motion of all repelling cycles contained in the Julia set, and combined with prior work of Berteloot, Bianchi, Brévard, Buff and Dupont this yields a complete stability-bifurcation dichotomy for arbitrary families.
conclusion: The stability-bifurcation theory for holomorphic endomorphisms of projective space is thereby completed, with analogous conclusions for holomorphic families of large-degree polynomial-like maps.

title: Sublinear Metric Distortion For Matching
authors: Moses Charikar, Alireza Haqi, Jabari Hastings, Yichen Huang, Prasanna Ramakrishnan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study metric distortion in one-sided matching. Given [MATH] agents and [MATH] items in an unknown metric space, our goal is to match agents to items so that the total distance between matched pairs is small. However, instead of direct access to the distances in the metric, we are only given each agent's ranking of the items by distance. What is the smallest worst-case approximation factor (called the distortion) that a mechanism can guarantee in expectation? Despite significant interest over the last decade, the best-known guarantee has been the [MATH] distortion of Random Serial Dictatorship since the beginning. We give a matching mechanism with distortion [MATH], the first sublinear upper bound. The key idea is to use a partial matching derived from a truncated version of either Random Serial Dictatorship or the Probabilistic Serial rule. We then complete this matching using a new, general-purpose cluster completion algorithm that ensures unmatched agents receive nearby items. Along the way, we pin down the optimal distortion of Random Serial Dictatorship and Probabilistic Serial up to logarithmic and constant factors, respectively, and give improved lower bounds for truthful mechanisms.
tldr: The paper gives the first sublinear worst-case distortion mechanism for one-sided matching from ordinal preference rankings over an unknown metric space.
motivation: Metric distortion in matching has been stuck at the linear O(n) guarantee of Random Serial Dictatorship for a decade, so improving the worst-case approximation is a natural open problem.
method: A partial matching is built from a truncated random serial dictatorship or probabilistic serial rule, then extended to a full matching via a new general-purpose cluster completion algorithm that assigns nearby items to unmatched agents.
result: The authors obtain a sublinear distortion guarantee, pin down the distortion of Random Serial Dictatorship and Probabilistic Serial up to logarithmic and constant factors, and prove improved lower bounds for truthful mechanisms.
conclusion: The work breaks the long-standing linear distortion barrier in ordinal matching and provides tighter characterizations of classical mechanisms.

title: When File Ingestion Misleads Language Models: Measuring And Mitigating Divergences In Office Documents
authors: Penghui Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Office documents are now routinely uploaded to large language models (LLMs) for processing. However, an LLM does not always see what a human sees, because it typically reads the text that an extractor produces from the document's underlying Office Open XML (OOXML) files. Depending on the implementation, extractors differ in which OOXML parts they read and how they interpret them, so their output can differ from what Office applications display. For example, by slightly shifting the positions of text boxes on a slide, an adversary can swap the order in which the model reads them while the slide looks unchanged. We show that this extraction divergence is an attack surface for LLM applications. In this work, we first measure what an adversary can exploit by analyzing the widely used extractors that LLM applications rely on. By combining static source code analysis with dynamic analysis, we identify 19 OOXML channels where extractors read content a human cannot see and 12 where they drop content a human can. We also find that widely used extractors ignore display formatting and reading order, so even visible content reaches the model in a different form. Building on these findings, we construct five attacks that lead the model to interpret a document differently from a human reviewer, without injecting any instruction. We test the attacks on four major chat assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Microsoft 365 Copilot) and four coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity, and GitHub Copilot CLI), and every one of them is misled by at least one attack. Finally, we propose Prism, a lightweight defense that reconstructs the human view from the OOXML specification before passing the text to the model. Prism also generalizes to unseen attack payloads.
tldr: The paper shows that OOXML text extractors used by LLM applications diverge from what humans see in Office documents, creating an attack surface, and proposes a defense called Prism.
motivation: LLMs read extracted text rather than rendered documents, so mismatches between extractor output and human-visible content can be exploited to mislead models without any explicit prompt injection.
method: The authors combine static source-code analysis and dynamic analysis of widely used extractors to enumerate OOXML channels where hidden content is read or visible content dropped, then construct five attacks tested against four chat assistants and four coding agents, and build Prism, a defense reconstructing the human view from the OOXML specification.
result: They identify 19 channels where extractors read invisible content and 12 where they drop visible content, and every tested assistant and coding agent is misled by at least one attack; Prism mitigates these attacks and generalizes to unseen payloads.
conclusion: File-ingestion divergence is a practical security weakness for LLM document processing, and specification-based reconstruction of the rendered view offers a lightweight defense.

title: Enforcing Accountable Disclosure In Confidential Ai
authors: Shumpei Shiina, Haruka Takahashi, Kento Sasaki, Takuya Hayashi, Tsubasa Takahashi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Advances in CPU and GPU confidential computing enable confidential AI, allowing LLMs to process user prompts without exposing them to service providers or infrastructure operators. However, AI agents often need to send prompt-derived information to external services, and providers may also require limited disclosure for safety monitoring and failure diagnosis. We propose CORDE, a system for confidential virtual machines (CVMs) designed to satisfy the principle of Confine or Declare: user-derived data is confined by default, but when necessary, it may leave the CVM only after being "declared." To "declare" data is to record its exact contents, recipient, and stated reason in a user-accessible, tamper-evident declaration log. To put this principle into practice, we present an integrated system design that combines per-user information-flow control in Rust with a TEE-based ledger and remote attestation. Our evaluation on an NVIDIA H100 GPU shows that declaration before disclosure adds little overhead in task latency, about 0.5% on the AppWorld agent benchmark. CORDE provides a basis for accountable disclosure of user data, supporting responsible and transparent data management in AI services.
tldr: CORDE is a confidential-VM system that enforces a 'Confine or Declare' principle, requiring user-derived data to be logged in a tamper-evident declaration ledger before leaving the enclave.
motivation: Confidential AI enclaves protect prompts from providers, but agents must still disclose prompt-derived data to external services and safety monitors, creating a need for accountability mechanisms rather than absolute confinement.
method: The authors combine per-user information-flow control written in Rust with a TEE-based append-only ledger and remote attestation, deployed on an NVIDIA H100 GPU confidential VM.
result: Declaration-before-disclosure adds roughly 0.5% task latency overhead on the AppWorld agent benchmark, indicating near-negligible performance cost.
conclusion: The system offers a practical foundation for accountable, transparent handling of user data in confidential AI services.

title: Pimrop: A Feasibility Study Of Return-Oriented Programming On Commercial Processing-in-Memory Architectures
authors: William C. Tegge, Shouzhi Fang, Alex K. Jones
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Processing-in-Memory places small programmable cores on the memory device, where they execute beside the DRAM banks and beyond the control-flow defenses that protect host programs. The security of this in-memory code is an attack surface that remains largely unstudied. We present PIMROP, to our knowledge the first demonstrated code-reuse attack on a commercial Processing in-Memory ISA. We show that return-oriented programming is feasible on a real, commercially shipped PIM instruction set, the UPMEM DPU, whose DRAM Processing Units run C compiled by a dedicated LLVM toolchain. We build Galileo-for-DPU, a gadget scanner adapted to the DPU's fixed-width, 8-byte-aligned RISC encoding, and run it entirely on the UPMEM functional simulator in a reproducible Docker and VM environment. We find the runtime library that every kernel links already yields 517 non-trivial gadgets covering all five canonical ROP primitive classes, and all 13 PrIM benchmarks we scanned carry gadgets as well. We then demonstrate two verified end-to-end attacks, each reproducible on 10 of 10 runs. In the first, a stack buffer overflow in a DPU kernel overwrites the saved return address and diverts control into a routine that copies a secret into host-readable memory. In the second, we leak the same secret using a chain of reused gadgets alone, without diverting control into any such routine. We further show that two standard defenses--stack canaries and _FORTIFY_SOURCE-style bounds-check fortification--fail on the DPU in ways specific to the platform (misplaced canary, silently inactive wrapper), and we verify a bounds-checked DMA that stops the attack on 10 of 10 runs with no effect on benign requests. To enable further research on PIM security, we open-source Galileo-for-DPU and our testing harness at [URL].
tldr: PIMROP demonstrates the first code-reuse (return-oriented programming) attack on a commercial Processing-in-Memory ISA, the UPMEM DPU, and evaluates defenses against it.
motivation: Processing-in-Memory cores execute code beside DRAM banks outside host control-flow defenses, creating an unstudied attack surface for in-memory code security.
method: The authors build Galileo-for-DPU, a gadget scanner adapted to the DPU's fixed-width 8-byte-aligned RISC encoding, and run it on the UPMEM functional simulator within a reproducible Docker/VM environment to enumerate usable ROP gadgets.
result: The standard runtime library yields 517 non-trivial gadgets spanning all five canonical ROP primitive classes, and two end-to-end attacks (return-address overwrite and pure gadget-chain secret leak) succeed in 10 of 10 runs; stack canaries and _FORTIFY_SOURCE fail, while a bounds-checked DMA blocks the attack without harming benign requests.
conclusion: ROP is feasible on commercially shipped PIM hardware, standard host-style defenses are inadequate, and platform-aware mitigations are needed; the authors open-source their tooling to support further PIM security research.

title: Securing Web Agents With The Compile-Then-Execute Paradigm
authors: Annabella Chow, Jinhao Zhu, Sylvie Venuto, Abdulaziz Alharbi, Basel Alomair, Raluca Popa, David Wagner, Julien Piet
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web agents commonly follow the ReAct paradigm, selecting each action from runtime observations that inherently mix trusted and untrusted content. This design makes their control flow vulnerable to prompt injections embedded in webpages. We introduce Baya, a compile-then-execute web agent designed to prevent prompt-injection-driven control-flow hijacking by design. Before accessing the live website, Baya compiles the user's request into an executable Python program that calls a Trusted Website API. The planning model does not observe live website content; only the compiled program processes it. Untrusted data may determine program values or select among branches defined during compilation, but it cannot redefine the user task or cause the model to synthesize new website operations at runtime. The Trusted Website API gives the compiler a unified view of the website's action space, enabling ahead-of-time planning without the stepwise action discovery required by reactive agents. Our evaluation across 581 valid WebArena Verified tasks shows that Baya achieves 77.8% aggregate utility, outperforming browser-only ReAct (55.1%) and API-enabled ReAct (66.7%). On WASP, a security benchmark for web agents, Baya achieves 0% attack success rate, compared with 16.2% for API-enabled ReAct and 25.5% for browser-only ReAct.
tldr: Baya is a compile-then-execute web agent architecture that compiles user requests into Python programs against a Trusted Website API before any live web access, structurally preventing prompt-injection-driven control-flow hijacking.
motivation: ReAct-style web agents interleave planning with runtime observations that mix trusted instructions and untrusted webpage content, leaving their control flow exposed to injected prompts embedded in web pages.
method: The user request is compiled ahead of time into an executable Python program calling a Trusted Website API, so the planning model never observes live untrusted content; untrusted data can only fill values or select pre-defined branches, not redefine tasks or synthesize new operations.
result: Across 581 valid WebArena Verified tasks Baya reaches 77.8% aggregate utility versus 55.1% (browser-only ReAct) and 66.7% (API-enabled ReAct), and achieves 0% attack success rate on the WASP security benchmark versus 16.2% and 25.5% respectively.
conclusion: Separating compilation from execution gives both higher task utility and by-design immunity to prompt-injection attacks, suggesting architectural rather than filter-based defences for web agents.

title: Two-Sided Screening In Quality-Differentiated Markets
authors: Yaohao Liu, Mengfan Ma, Mingyu Xiao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by digital marketplaces such as Uber and Airbnb, we study how a two-sided platform designs a menu of qualities, consumer prices, and provider wages. Consumers and providers self-select according to their private values and costs, so the platform must design its menu to attract consumers while inducing enough supply to meet their demand. We study this coordination problem over a continuous quality space, requiring supply to cover demand at every quality threshold. We formulate menu design as an optimization over trading distributions, which specify how much trade occurs at or above each quality. Through convexification of the technological cost function, we characterize the profit- and welfare-optimal trading distributions. This characterization shows how production technology alone can reduce menu size without sacrificing optimal profit or welfare, regardless of the type distributions, and determines when optimal menus can be finite. We then show that profit maximization can be highly efficient: under monotone hazard rate conditions on both sides, a profit-optimal menu achieves at least [MATH] of optimal social welfare. We next consider the practical setting in which the menu size is restricted to a prescribed number of offers. We establish how the restricted menu approximates the unrestricted optimum in profit. We develop an algorithm that computes a menu within this size limit in polynomial time. The computed menu simultaneously approximates the unrestricted optimal profit and social welfare with additive error.
tldr: The paper studies how two-sided digital platforms design menus of quality, consumer prices, and provider wages when both sides self-select on private values and costs.
motivation: Motivated by marketplaces like Uber and Airbnb, the authors aim to understand how a platform coordinates consumer demand and provider supply while choosing quality levels and prices.
method: The menu design problem is formulated as an optimization over trading distributions in a continuous quality space, solved via convexification of the cost function, with an additional polynomial-time algorithm for size-restricted menus.
result: Profit- and welfare-optimal trading distributions are characterized; production technology alone can shrink menu size without loss, and under monotone hazard rate conditions a profit-optimal menu attains at least a constant fraction of optimal social welfare.
conclusion: The work provides a tractable characterization of optimal two-sided screening and shows restricted menus can approximate unrestricted optimal profit and welfare with additive error.

title: SenTrojan: Revealing Analog Hardware Trojan Attacks On Sensors
authors: Kun Wang, Ruochen Zhou, Wenjun Zhu, Shilin Xiao, Kai Wang, Chen Yan, Xiaoyu Ji, Wenyuan Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sensors bridge the physical and digital worlds, making their integrity critical to cyber-physical system security. Existing sensor attacks largely exploit unintended and sensor-specific physical vulnerabilities, limiting their generalizability and motivating a different threat model, i.e., whether an adversary can implant hidden attack surfaces into sensors before deployment. In this paper, we present SenTrojan, an analog hardware Trojan framework for sensors. SenTrojan embeds malicious functionality into analog signal circuitry commonly shared across diverse sensor architectures, and activates the hidden behavior through crafted external physical signals. Once activated, SenTrojan can induce sensor malfunctions ranging from permanent denial-of-service to static or dynamic spoofing. To achieve these effects under different architectural constraints, we introduce two complementary designs. The Logic-Rule-Driven (LRD) Trojan adds lightweight analog monitoring logic to detect trigger features such as frequency and amplitude, enabling reliable activation across various sensor types. The Physical-Effect-Driven (PED) Trojan targets sensors with exploitable native analog effects, e.g., nonlinearity and rectification, and realizes attacks with minimal component insertion. We evaluate SenTrojan on 14 sensors spanning 6 transduction principles and demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse real-world scenarios. Overall, SenTrojan achieves an average successful trigger rate above 95%, maintains over 97% similarity to benign behavior, incurs zero false-trigger rate for LRD designs, and introduces less than 5% average deviation in drift, noise floor, and response time. To our knowledge, this work is the first systematic study of analog sensor Trojans, broadening sensor security from unintended physical vulnerabilities to intentional supply-chain compromise.
tldr: SenTrojan introduces an analog hardware Trojan framework that implants hidden malicious functionality into sensor signal circuitry, enabling denial-of-service and spoofing attacks triggered by crafted physical signals.
motivation: Existing sensor attacks rely on unintended, sensor-specific physical vulnerabilities, which limits their generality; the authors instead propose an intentional supply-chain threat model in which hidden attack surfaces are implanted before deployment.
method: Two complementary Trojan designs are developed: a Logic-Rule-Driven (LRD) design that adds lightweight analog monitoring logic to detect trigger features such as frequency and amplitude, and a Physical-Effect-Driven (PED) design that exploits native analog effects like nonlinearity and rectification with minimal component insertion.
result: Evaluated on 14 sensors spanning 6 transduction principles, SenTrojan achieves over 95% average trigger success, more than 97% behavioral similarity to benign sensors, zero false triggers for LRD designs, and under 5% average deviation in drift, noise floor, and response time.
conclusion: The work is presented as the first systematic study of analog sensor Trojans, extending sensor security from unintended physical vulnerabilities to deliberate supply-chain compromise.

title: Regret Bounds For Market Making With Persistent Orders
authors: Nicol\`o Cesa-Bianchi, Tommaso Cesari, Roberto Colomboni, Luigi Foscari, Vinayak Pathak
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study adversarial market making with orders that remain active until execution. The maker operates on two markets: a primary market where orders are made and a secondary market where the resulting positions are hedged. In each round, the maker posts a quote on the primary market before observing both primary and secondary market prices. An order executes when the primary price reaches its quote, and the resulting position is immediately offset at the secondary price. When both price sequences are chosen by an adversary over [MATH] rounds, we give a simple deterministic policy with regret of order [MATH] against the best fixed quote (static comparator) and [MATH] against the best quote for each submission date (dynamic comparator), plus two terms measuring exposure to future primary and secondary prices. These rates remain optimal even when both exposure terms vanish and lower bounds show that the exposure terms are necessary. Our policy naturally extends to simultaneous bids and asks, where we show that static and dynamic regret are both characterized (up to constant factors) by the exposures terms (where the primary price exposure [MATH] now accounts for both bids and asks) and a term of order [MATH]. Our policy is simple, efficient and fully parameterless. We extend this setting by demonstrating how natural assumptions on the price processes lead to improved guarantees without changing the policy.
tldr: The paper derives regret bounds for adversarial market making with persistent limit orders across a primary market and a hedging secondary market.
motivation: Market makers posting quotes that remain active until execution face adversarial price sequences and hedging exposure, and principled performance guarantees for such strategies are lacking.
method: The authors design a simple deterministic, parameterless online learning policy and prove upper and lower bounds on static and dynamic regret, including exposure terms to future primary and secondary prices, extending to simultaneous bids and asks.
result: The policy achieves regret of order sqrt(T)-type rates against static and dynamic comparators, with matching lower bounds showing the exposure terms are necessary; these rates are characterized up to constants in the two-sided (bid/ask) setting.
conclusion: Near-optimal, efficient guarantees are established for adversarial market making with persistent orders, and mild assumptions on price processes yield improved bounds without modifying the policy.

title: Network Intrusion Forensic Detection System With Explainable Artificial Intelligence And Digital Chain Of Custody
authors: Carmen Pellicer Jose Luis Vela Alonso
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deploying an explainable intrusion detection model from a validated laboratory setting into a forensic workflow requires guarantees that benchmarks do not test: that the certified model is the exact artifact applied to a case, that heterogeneous evidence can be classified reliably, and that every step is verifiable. We present MODEXRE, a forensic pipeline that extends a previously validated synthetic-data-trained XGBoost classifier with SHAP explainability (arXiv:2607.00763) into a dual-mode architecture: a Laboratory mode, where models are trained and certified on public and synthetic data, and a Formal mode, where a frozen, hash-verified model performs inference on case evidence under a SHA-256 hash-chained chain of custody. Suricata alerts, CEF firewall logs and packet captures are normalized through OCSF. Four design decisions, each triggered by an observed failure, shaped the architecture: a timestamp leak that inflated Kitsune performance (F1-macro 0.984, 0.662 after correction); a feature-coverage gap that made the 78-feature reference model misclassify a real SSH alert; causal temporal flow aggregation, which raised Kitsune multiclass F1-macro from 0.394 to 0.932; and a certification defect, exposed only by a real packet capture, whereby the pipeline had always trained a binary classifier. After correction, the same capture went from 100% of events flagged as malicious to 87% classified as Normal, with the scanning host identified as Reconnaissance. The default four-class certified model reaches F1-macro = 0.9538 on CICIDS2017-derived evidence; the recertified 18-category model reaches 0.6214, reflecting the real multiclass task. Chain-of-custody verification, model integrity hashing and per-prediction SHAP explanations are reported as measured outcomes.
tldr: MODEXRE is a forensic intrusion-detection pipeline that wraps a certified XGBoost/SHAP classifier in a dual-mode (laboratory vs. formal) architecture with SHA-256 hash-chained chain of custody for case evidence.
motivation: Moving an explainable intrusion-detection model from a validated lab benchmark into real forensic workflows requires guarantees benchmarks ignore: that the certified artifact is exactly the one applied to a case, that heterogeneous evidence (Suricata alerts, CEF logs, packet captures) is handled reliably, and that every step is verifiable.
method: The authors extend a synthetic-data-trained XGBoost classifier with SHAP explainability into a dual-mode pipeline, normalizing evidence through OCSF, performing causal temporal flow aggregation, hash-verifying frozen models, and recording per-prediction explanations under a SHA-256 hash-chained chain of custody; four architecture decisions were each driven by an observed failure (timestamp leakage, feature-coverage gap, temporal aggregation, binary-vs-multiclass certification defect).
result: The default four-class certified model reaches F1-macro 0.9538 on CICIDS2017-derived evidence while the recertified 18-category model reaches 0.6214; causal temporal aggregation raised Kitsune multiclass F1-macro from 0.394 to 0.932, and after correcting the certification defect a real packet capture went from 100% malicious flags to 87% Normal with the scanning host labeled Reconnaissance.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that explainability plus cryptographic chain of custody and model-integrity hashing can make ML-based intrusion detection auditable for forensic use, and highlights how realistic multiclass evaluation exposes inflated benchmark performance.

title: Beyond The Landing Page: Website Blocking, Tracker Visibility, And Human Alignment In Automated Web Crawls
authors: A H M Nazmus Sakib, Mahsin Bin Akram, Raveen Wijewickrama, Igor Bilogrevic, Murtuza Jadliwala
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web tracking studies largely rely on automated crawlers, yet their measurements can differ from what people encounter while browsing. Conventional crawlers follow predefined navigation rules, whereas LLM-driven agents decide how to navigate and interact with websites, potentially changing the tracking they encounter. We compare agentic and non-agentic crawlers to examine how websites respond to them, what tracking they record, and how closely their observations match human browsing. Across 2,000 popular websites, we evaluate different navigation strategies, automation frameworks, and stealth configurations, alongside browsing data from 26 participants. We find that website denials increase beyond landing pages for standard browser automation, while a detection-resistant automation framework largely prevents this escalation without increasing recorded tracking.
