On the same URLs, agentic crawlers record tracking activity from 1.5-1.7 times as many third-party organizations, particularly on consent-managed pages. Agentic crawlers recover 82-87% of tracker organizations observed by participants, compared with 58-68% for non-agentic crawlers, yet roughly half of their own observations are absent from human participant visits. These findings show that avoiding website interventions, increasing tracking visibility, and achieving closer agreement with human observations do not necessarily go hand in hand, highlighting the need to select and validate crawlers according to the measurement objective.
tldr: The paper compares agentic (LLM-driven) and non-agentic web crawlers on 2,000 popular websites to measure how site blocking, third-party tracking visibility, and agreement with real human browsing differ between them.
motivation: Web tracking studies depend on automated crawlers, but crawler measurements may not reflect what human users actually experience, and LLM-driven agents may navigate and trigger tracking differently than rule-based crawlers.
method: The authors crawl 2,000 popular websites using varied navigation strategies, automation frameworks, and stealth configurations, collecting browsing data from 26 human participants as a ground-truth baseline for comparison.
result: Standard automation faces escalating denials beyond landing pages while a detection-resistant framework avoids this; agentic crawlers observe 1.5-1.7x more third-party tracker organizations and recover 82-87% of human-observed trackers (vs. 58-68% for non-agentic), though about half their observations are absent from human visits.
conclusion: Avoiding site interventions, maximizing tracking visibility, and matching human browsing do not coincide, so crawlers must be selected and validated according to the specific measurement objective.

title: Analysis Of Local Open-Weight Llm Agents On Vulnerability-Reproduction Tasks
authors: Jorge Garc\'ia-Carrasco, Javier Sanchis, \'alvaro Navarro, Alejandro Mat\'e, Juan Trujillo
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-weight language models that fit on a single consumer GPU are becoming capable on a growing range of tasks, and they matter because they can run locally without sending the code to a hosted service. Vulnerability reproduction, turning a vulnerability description into an input that crashes the vulnerable build, is a natural target for them, since it is an automated analysis task closer to test generation than to code comprehension and it runs against a build that must be executed rather than read. In order to assess whether current models can perform it, we evaluate twelve configurations of local models, spanning three generations, two architectures and three quantization levels, on ten CyberGym vulnerability-reproduction tasks, three runs each under one harness, and release the full artefact. We show that every configuration, down to the 4B model, solves most of the six easier tasks, and configurations separate only on the remaining four. For the harder tasks, the 27B model is required. Quantization did not change what the models solved in any matched pair, but it changed how fast they got there, and the mixture of experts reached the same scores in less wall clock. We also examine the agent trajectories. Almost every run we examined, including those that fail, names the vulnerable function and states the correct hypothesis, and what separates a solved task from an unsolved one is whether that hypothesis becomes a working input.
tldr: This paper benchmarks twelve local open-weight LLM configurations on vulnerability-reproduction tasks, measuring whether they can turn a vulnerability description into a crashing input.
motivation: Open-weight models that run locally on consumer GPUs are increasingly capable and avoid sending proprietary code to hosted services, making them attractive for automated security-analysis tasks such as vulnerability reproduction.
method: Twelve configurations spanning three model generations, two architectures, and three quantization levels are evaluated on ten CyberGym vulnerability-reproduction tasks, with three runs each under a single harness, plus analysis of agent trajectories.
result: All configurations down to the 4B model solve most of the six easier tasks and only separate on the four harder ones, where the 27B model is required; quantization did not change which tasks were solved but affected speed, and the mixture-of-experts model matched scores in less wall-clock time.
conclusion: Local open-weight LLM agents are largely capable on easier vulnerability-reproduction tasks, and the key differentiator between success and failure is whether a correct vulnerability hypothesis is converted into a working crashing input.

title: Comparative Analysis Of Numerical Methods For X-ray 3d Reconstruction From Sparse Views
authors: Konstantinos K. Delibasis Melitine N. Bardi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reconstruction of three-dimensional vascular structures from a limited number of X-ray projections is a severely underdetermined and ill-conditioned inverse problem. This work presents a unified matrix-free computational framework for evaluating iterative numerical methods for sparse-view cone-beam tomography. Forward and backprojection are implemented from ray-voxel intersection lengths computed with the Amanatides-Woo traversal algorithm, avoiding explicit construction of the large sparse system matrix. We systematically compare ART, SART, SIRT, gradient descent (GD), and Krylov subspace methods, including Conjugate Gradient, LSQR, and GMRES. The common matrix-free operators and geometry are used for all methods, allowing consistent comparisons under matched conditions. Particular emphasis is placed on gradient scaling using scalar step sizes, Jacobi preconditioning, and diagonal Hessian majorization, together with L1, Tikhonov, and total variation regularization. Numerical experiments use five three-dimensional coronary vessel models reconstructed from ten simulated X-ray projections under noise and scattering conditions, and are extended to real X-ray projections of a static thin-vessel phantom. Performance is evaluated in terms of convergence, computational cost, volumetric overlap, contrast-to-noise ratio, vessel diameter and centerline errors, and projection consistency at an unseen viewing angle. The results show that total-variation-regularized gradient descent with diagonal majorization provides the best overall reconstruction performance within the investigated computational budgets. By contrast, the tested Krylov implementations achieve limited geometric recovery despite higher computational cost. These findings emphasize the importance of appropriate gradient scaling and regularization for stable and computationally efficient sparse-view tomographic reconstruction.
tldr: A matrix-free numerical comparison of iterative tomographic reconstruction algorithms (ART, SART, SIRT, GD, Krylov methods) for sparse-view 3D X-ray reconstruction of vascular structures.
motivation: Reconstructing 3D vascular structures from few X-ray projections is a severely ill-posed inverse problem, and practitioners lack consistent head-to-head comparisons of iterative solvers under matched conditions.
method: Forward/backprojection operators are built matrix-free from Amanatides-Woo ray-voxel intersection lengths, and ART, SART, SIRT, gradient descent, CG, LSQR, and GMRES are compared with scalar step sizes, Jacobi preconditioning, diagonal Hessian majorization, and L1/Tikhonov/total-variation regularization on simulated coronary vessel models and a real phantom.
result: TV-regularized gradient descent with diagonal majorization gave the best overall reconstruction, while Krylov methods showed limited geometric recovery despite higher computational cost.
conclusion: Appropriate gradient scaling and regularization are key to stable, efficient sparse-view tomographic reconstruction.

title: Quartic Polynomial Differential Systems With Three Disjoint Invariant Circles
authors: Jaume Llibre Chen Cao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the normal forms of real planar polynomial differential systems of degree at most four with three prescribed pairwise disjoint invariant circles, covering all configurations of their centers. None of the prescribed circles is a limit cycle in the concentric case or in the coaxial case with three distinct centers, where the pairwise radical axes coincide. When exactly two centers coincide, or when the three centers are distinct and collinear and the circles are non-coaxial, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for all three circles to be algebraic limit cycles, which are necessarily hyperbolic. For non-collinear centers, we give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions for all three circles to be periodic orbits and for all three to be hyperbolic algebraic limit cycles. Each of the four configurations with non-collinear centers is realized by a coprime quartic polynomial differential system with three hyperbolic circular limit cycles.
tldr: The paper classifies quartic planar polynomial differential systems that have three pairwise disjoint invariant circles and determines when these circles are limit cycles.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the normal-form classification of planar polynomial differential systems with prescribed invariant algebraic curves, specifically three disjoint circles, across all center configurations.
method: They derive normal forms for real planar quartic polynomial differential systems with three prescribed disjoint invariant circles and analyze the resulting configurations of centers and radical axes.
result: They provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the three circles to be hyperbolic algebraic limit cycles in several configurations and show realizability by coprime quartic systems with three hyperbolic circular limit cycles.
conclusion: The work gives a complete classification of quartic systems with three disjoint invariant circles and identifies configurations supporting hyperbolic circular limit cycles.

title: Improving Hydrofoil Efficiency Through Simulation-Driven Design Optimization
authors: Ante Sikirica, Ivana Lu\v{c}in, Marta Alvir, Tin Matulja
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Foil windsurfing is a sport in which competitors fine-tune their setup to optimize performance under varying environmental conditions. However, such adjustments are typically guided by intuition. This paper presents a methodology for improving hydrofoil design using computational fluid dynamics. First, structured light scanning was used to obtain the geometry of a conventional hydrofoil. Subsequently, five derived designs have been explored, inspired by advancements in airplane wing design. Following this, a preliminary design was selected, and a design of experiments approach was implemented. Generated simulation data were used to train a machine learning surrogate, which is ultimately used in the multi-objective design optimization. While the surrogate-based approach yielded promising results, it was limited to exploring a restricted set of design parameters. To overcome this constraint, additional improvements were attained through adjoint optimization, demonstrating that comparable performance can be achieved with a distinctly different hydrofoil design. Finally, the conventional design was refined through adjoint optimization. Notably, adjoint optimization yielded a 15% increase in efficiency. The results suggest that both proposed approaches can produce novel hydrofoil designs capable of outperforming the original configuration under specific conditions; however, due to its inherent flexibility, the adjoint approach with realistic constraints offers more freedom in the design exploration process.
tldr: The paper develops a simulation-driven optimization methodology combining CFD, machine-learning surrogates, and adjoint optimization to improve foil windsurfing hydrofoil efficiency.
motivation: Hydrofoil setups in foil windsurfing are typically tuned by intuition, so the authors aim to provide a systematic computational design approach inspired by aircraft wing design.
method: Structured light scanning captures a conventional hydrofoil geometry; five derived designs are explored, a design-of-experiments study trains a surrogate model for multi-objective optimization, and adjoint optimization is used for further refinement.
result: The surrogate-based approach gives promising but parameter-limited improvements, while adjoint optimization yields a 15% efficiency increase and reveals alternative high-performance hydrofoil designs.
conclusion: Both approaches can outperform the original hydrofoil under specific conditions, but adjoint optimization with realistic constraints offers greater design freedom and is the more flexible route.

title: Accessibility Of Collapsed Anosov Flow
authors: Ra\'ul Ures Ziqiang Feng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every [MATH] collapsed Anosov flow on a closed three-manifold with non-virtually-solvable fundamental group is accessible. No transitivity or nonwandering assumption is required, and the collapsing map need not satisfy the strong-collapse conditions. We also prove that every three-dimensional collapsed Anosov flow for which no positive iterate is a discretized Anosov flow is accessible.
tldr: The paper proves accessibility of collapsed Anosov flows on closed three-manifolds under certain fundamental-group and non-discretization conditions.
motivation: Accessibility is a structural property in the theory of Anosov flows, and the authors aim to establish it for collapsed Anosov flows without requiring transitivity, nonwandering, or strong-collapse assumptions.
method: The proof is carried out in the setting of three-dimensional smooth dynamical systems and uses techniques from the geometric theory of Anosov flows and foliations.
result: Every collapsed Anosov flow on a closed three-manifold with non-virtually-solvable fundamental group is accessible, and accessibility also holds when no positive iterate is a discretized Anosov flow.
conclusion: The results extend accessibility theorems to broader classes of collapsed Anosov flows, removing several standard hypotheses.

title: Constraint-Aware Evaluation Of Reinforcement Learning And Unsupervised Anomaly Detection For Security Operations Alert Triage
authors: Rifny Rachman Radityo Ghifiardi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Security Operations Centers (SOCs) must identify real threats from large alert streams, but limited analyst capacity means that unnecessary escalations can delay more serious investigations. Existing studies often frame SOC alert triage as classification or anomaly detection, but both views are incomplete for production SOCs, where the central problem is selecting alerts worth escalating under limited capacity, asymmetric error costs, and workload constraints. This paper addresses that gap by formalizing alert triage as a constrained decision problem and evaluating three approaches: an offline reinforcement learning policy trained on alert embeddings, an Isolation Forest model built on operational features, and an autoencoder trained on historical benign alerts. These methods represent different triage assumptions: learning actions from reward, isolating unusual operational patterns, and detecting deviations from benign behavior. We evaluate all methods on 74,909 analyst-labeled production alerts under a strict temporal split and benign-escalation constraint. Because the test set contains 503 unique feature patterns, we primarily rank clusters of similar alerts. At the main operating point, all three methods satisfy the constraint, with the reinforcement learning policy achieving the lowest benign-escalation fraction at 0.000, compared with 0.007 for the autoencoder and 0.041 for Isolation Forest. The methods also prioritize largely different alert clusters, showing complementary rather than redundant coverage. These results suggest that production SOC triage can benefit from constraint-aware evaluation and combined or adaptive deployment of different model families.
tldr: The paper formalizes Security Operations Center alert triage as a capacity-constrained decision problem and compares offline reinforcement learning, Isolation Forest, and autoencoder approaches on production alert data.
motivation: SOC analysts face overwhelming alert volumes and limited capacity, so the real problem is not mere classification or anomaly detection but deciding which alerts are worth escalating under asymmetric error costs and workload constraints.
method: The authors train an offline RL policy on alert embeddings, an Isolation Forest on operational features, and an autoencoder on historical benign alerts, then evaluate them on 74,909 analyst-labeled production alerts with a strict temporal split and a benign-escalation constraint, ranking clusters of similar alerts.
result: At the main operating point all three methods satisfied the constraint, with the RL policy giving the lowest benign-escalation fraction (0.000) versus 0.007 for the autoencoder and 0.041 for Isolation Forest, while the methods prioritized largely different alert clusters.
conclusion: Constraint-aware evaluation and combined or adaptive deployment of complementary model families can improve production SOC triage.

title: KVGuard: A Kv Cache Safety Checker For Llm Serving Systems
authors: Jonguk Cheong, Myungbin Hwang, Eulgyu Kim, Byoungyoung Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern LLM serving systems manage the KV cache through PagedAttention, a custom GPU allocator that partitions a single CUDA-allocated region into fixed-size physical blocks and maps each request to those blocks through a CPU-built block table. This block-based design exposes a previously unstudied class of memory safety bugs in the KV cache, including double-free, use-after-free, out-of-bounds access, uninitialized read, and permission violation, which silently corrupt outputs or break request isolation without ever crashing the system. Existing memory sanitizers cannot detect them, because they reason about CUDA-level addresses rather than KV cache blocks, requests, and block tables, and their redzone- and quarantine-based designs do not fit the scarce GPU memory budget of LLM serving. This paper presents KVGuard, the first systematic memory-safety abstraction for KV cache management in LLM serving systems. KVGuard maintains a compact shadow block for each physical KV block, recording per-request permission and per-entry initialization, and uses this metadata to perform five safety checks across the PagedAttention workflow, spanning CPU allocation, block table construction and translation, and GPU-side block table lookup and KV entry access. Each check fires at the boundary that introduced the violation, enabling early detection during development rather than reporting downstream output corruption many requests later. A prototype of KVGuard on vLLM and SGLang covers all 29 historical real-world KV cache safety bugs collected from the two systems' patch histories. KVGuard further found 8 previously unknown safety violations while reporting no false positives. It adds 3.0% and 7.4% geomean TPOT overhead on Qwen 2.5 14B on vLLM and SGLang and at most 0.11% of the KV cache in memory overhead, two orders of magnitude below NVIDIA Compute Sanitizer on the same workloads.
tldr: KVGuard is a memory-safety checker for KV-cache block management in LLM serving systems built on PagedAttention (vLLM, SGLang).
motivation: Block-based KV cache allocation exposes double-free, use-after-free, out-of-bounds, uninitialized-read, and permission-violation bugs that silently corrupt outputs and break request isolation without crashing, and existing CUDA-level sanitizers cannot detect them within GPU memory budgets.
method: The authors introduce a shadow-block abstraction tracking per-request permissions and per-entry initialization, and run five safety checks across CPU allocation, block-table construction/translation, and GPU-side block-table lookup and KV entry access.
result: The prototype covers all 29 historical real-world KV-cache safety bugs from vLLM and SGLang patch histories, finds 8 previously unknown violations with no false positives, and adds 3.0%/7.4% geomean TPOT overhead with at most 0.11% KV-cache memory overhead.
conclusion: KVGuard provides early, boundary-localized detection of KV-cache memory-safety violations at far lower cost than NVIDIA Compute Sanitizer, but it is a systems-security contribution with no connection to quantum information science.

title: One Strategic Woman: Sharp Ranks And A Persistent Core
authors: Ron Kupfer
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a balanced random stable-marriage market, one fixed woman manipulates men-proposing deferred acceptance to obtain her best attainable partner. We prove that the women's expected average true partner rank is asymptotic to [MATH], improving the previous [MATH] bound, while the men's is asymptotic to [MATH]. The men's and women's average ranks, normalized by [MATH] and [MATH], converge jointly in distribution to [MATH], where [MATH] is uniform on [MATH]. Under optimal truthful truncation, the span of women's average ranks within the reported stable core, divided by [MATH], converges in distribution to [MATH].
tldr: The paper analyzes strategic manipulation in balanced random stable-marriage markets, deriving sharp asymptotic rank distributions and persistent-core behavior for a single manipulating woman.
motivation: It aims to quantify how a fixed woman can benefit from manipulating men-proposing deferred acceptance and to sharpen asymptotic bounds on average partner ranks.
method: The author studies random stable-marriage markets with one strategic woman, derives asymptotic average true ranks, and proves joint distributional convergence of normalized men's and women's average ranks under optimal truthful truncation.
result: Women's expected average true partner rank is shown to have an improved asymptotic formula, men's rank asymptotic is derived, and the normalized rank statistics converge jointly to a uniform limit; the span of women's average ranks in the reported stable core also has a limiting distribution.
conclusion: The work provides sharp asymptotic and distributional results for strategic stable matching, showing a persistent-core effect and improved rank bounds.

title: Explainable Anomaly Detection In 5g Networks Through Continuous Time Graphs
authors: Thomas Hoger (LAAS, Laas-Sara, Laas-Risc), Philippe Owezarski
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: 5G networks increasingly resemble distributed systems in their design. It then becomes crucial to move beyond traditional network-based detection methods and to explore alternative approaches. In this work, we propose a formalization of 5G network exchanges as a dynamic graph, on which we apply techniques from the field of graph-based learning to detect anomalies effectively. This representation allows for fine-grained analysis of packet-level semantic content, while simultaneously capturing sequential and topological contexts, both of which are essential for identifying sophisticated and multi-stage attacks. To assess the effectiveness of this formalism, we evaluate it with the most popular dynamic graph models, demonstrating its potential for 5G anomaly detection.
tldr: The paper proposes modeling 5G network traffic as a continuous-time dynamic graph and applies graph-learning models for explainable anomaly detection.
motivation: 5G networks are increasingly distributed and complex, making traditional network-based anomaly detection insufficient for sophisticated multi-stage attacks.
method: The authors formalize packet-level 5G exchanges as a dynamic graph and evaluate popular dynamic graph learning models for anomaly detection.
result: The dynamic-graph formalism captures sequential and topological contexts and shows potential for effective 5G anomaly detection.
conclusion: Graph-based learning on continuous-time representations can support fine-grained, explainable anomaly detection in 5G networks.

title: A.s.e 2.0: Understanding How Repository Context Impacts The Security Of LLM-Generated Code
authors: Jiongchi Yu, Keke Lian, Junqing Wang, Zhikang Fan, Zhaoxuan Li, Yongheng Huang, Ziming Zhao, Dong Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.06294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) coding assistants and agents construct a repository context before generating code. For security-sensitive code, this context decides whether the model sees the project's safeguards (e.g., authorization checks) or insecure code to imitate. However, context construction is designed almost exclusively for functional correctness, and secure-code benchmarks treat the context as fixed, so how repository context affects the security of generated code remains unclear. We construct CASE-Bench, a benchmark of 145 repository-level tasks from real CVEs in 51 projects. Each task runs in Docker, has functional tests and a proof-of-concept exploit validated in both directions, and is annotated with the repository code that enforces or undermines its security. Using CASE-Bench, we compare 13 context construction methods and six controls with six LLMs, edit single context elements, and analyze coding-agent trajectories. We find that (1) functionality-oriented context raises the functional pass rate by up to 8.2 percentage points (pp) but the secure pass rate by at most 3.7 pp, (2) withholding a safeguard lowers the secure pass rate by up to 8.1 pp, while one inserted insecure exemplar raises correct-but-exploitable code by 6.3 pp, and (3) coding agents observe the relevant safeguard in only 27-36% of trajectories. These findings inform security-aware context construction and secure-code evaluation.
tldr: This paper introduces CASE-Bench, a benchmark of 145 repository-level tasks from real CVEs, to study how repository context construction impacts the security of LLM-generated code.
motivation: LLM coding assistants build repository context designed almost exclusively for functional correctness, and existing secure-code benchmarks treat context as fixed, leaving unclear how context selection affects code security.
method: The authors construct CASE-Bench with Dockerized tasks, functional tests, bidirectional-validated proof-of-concept exploits, and annotations of safeguarding code, then compare 13 context construction methods and six controls across six LLMs, edit individual context elements, and analyze agent trajectories.
result: Functionality-oriented context improves functional pass rates by up to 8.2 pp but secure pass rates by at most 3.7 pp; withholding a safeguard lowers secure pass rate by up to 8.1 pp, and a single insecure exemplar raises correct-but-exploitable code by 6.3 pp; agents observe the relevant safeguard in only 27-36% of trajectories.
conclusion: Repository context critically shapes the security of LLM-generated code, motivating security-aware context construction and secure-code evaluation practices.

title: Quantum Theory Of Damping: A New Approach To Temporal Evolution Of Density Operator Without The Rotating Wave Approximation
authors: A. Marashi Nasab, E. Ghasemian, M. K. Tavassoly
abstract: ArXiv:2611.05537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Lindblad master equation is the standard framework for describing dissipative dynamics of the open quantum system context. Its conventional derivation, however, relies on the rotating-wave approximation (RWA), which neglects the counter rotating terms in the system-reservoir interaction. Here, we derive a generalized Lindblad master equation beyond the RWA within the density operator formalism, retaining the full systemreservoir coupling. We consider two prototypical open quantum systems, a two-level atom and a single-mode quantized field, each interacting with thermal or squeezed reservoirs described by the Wigner-Weisskopf theory. The resulting master equations are applied to the evolution of representative physical observables and compared with the conventional RWA based formulation. We show that counter-rotating terms produce significant modifications to the dissipative dynamics and therefore cannot, in general, be neglected. For a thermal reservoir, increasing the mean thermal photon number, nth, enhances the decay of h{\sigma}^yi beyond the RWA but suppresses it within the RWA. Likewise, the evolution of h{\sigma}^zi exhibits opposite damping behavior with increasing {\Gamma}t and squeezing parameter r. These findings demonstrate the importance of including counter rotating terms for an accurate description of open quantum systems.
